title.en: Volume 41 Biographies 11: Wei Shu; Li Xi; Liu Shi; Gao Guang
title.raw: 卷四十一 列傳第十一 魏舒 李憙 劉寔 高光 Volume 41 Biographies 11: Wei Shu; Li Xi; Liu Shi; Gao Guang

sentences.zh: 魏舒，字陽元，任城樊人也。

translations.literal: Wei Shu, courtesy name Yangyuan, was a man of Fan in Rencheng.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Shu, whose courtesy name was Yangyuan, came from Fan in Rencheng commandery.

sentences.zh: 少孤，為外家寧氏所養。

translations.literal: In youth he was orphaned and was reared by his maternal family, the Ning clan.
translations.idiomatic: He lost his parents while still young and was brought up by his mother’s people, the Nings.

sentences.zh: 寧氏起宅，相宅者云：「當出貴甥。

translations.literal: When the Ning built a house, a geomancer said, “A noble nephew will come forth from this.”
translations.idiomatic: While the Nings were erecting a new residence, a geomancer declared, “This site will produce a distinguished nephew.”

sentences.zh: 」外祖母以魏氏甥小而慧，意謂應之。

translations.literal: ” His maternal grandmother, because the Wei nephew was small yet clever, thought it referred to him.
translations.idiomatic: His grandmother, noting that the Wei boy was young but bright, assumed the prophecy pointed to him.

sentences.zh: 舒曰：「當為外氏成此宅相。

translations.literal: Shu said, “I shall fulfill this house omen for the maternal clan.”
translations.idiomatic: Shu replied, “It falls to me to vindicate this reading of the house for my mother’s family.”

sentences.zh: 」久乃別居。

translations.literal: ” Only after a long while did he live apart.
translations.idiomatic: Only much later did he move out and establish a separate household.

sentences.zh: 身長八尺二寸，姿望秀偉，飲酒石餘，而遲鈍質樸，不為鄉親所重。

translations.literal: His body was eight chi two cun in height; his bearing was handsome and imposing; he drank more than a shi of wine; yet he was slow, dull, and plain, and was not esteemed by townsmen and kin.
translations.idiomatic: He stood eight chi two cun tall, carried himself with striking presence, and could put away more than a shi of wine at a sitting, yet he seemed slow and unpolished, so neighbors and relatives thought little of him.

sentences.zh: 從叔父吏部郎衡，有名當世，亦不之知，使守水碓，每歎曰：「舒堪數百戶長，我願畢矣！

translations.literal: His paternal uncle once removed, Heng, Director of the Ministry of Personnel, had fame in the age, yet did not recognize him either, and had him guard the water mill, often sighing, “Shu suffices for chief of several hundred households; my wish is fulfilled!”
translations.idiomatic: His father’s cousin Heng, a celebrated Director in the Ministry of Personnel, likewise failed to see his worth and set him to mind the water-powered mill, sighing, “Shu is good enough to head a few hundred households—that would satisfy me!”

sentences.zh: 」舒亦不以介意。

translations.literal: ” Shu also did not take it to heart.
translations.idiomatic: Shu himself was untroubled by such slighting treatment.

sentences.zh: 不修常人之節，不為皎曆之事，每欲容才長物，終不顯人之短。

translations.literal: He did not cultivate ordinary men’s punctilios, did not do ostentatious display matters; he always wished to accommodate talent and let things grow, and to the end did not expose others’ shortcomings.
translations.idiomatic: He spurned petty conventional propriety and flashy self-advertisement; he preferred to make room for others’ abilities and strengths and never paraded their faults.

sentences.zh: 性好騎射，著韋衣。

translations.literal: By nature he loved riding and archery and wore leather garments.
translations.idiomatic: He loved horseback archery and habitually dressed in tough leather hunting clothes.

sentences.zh: 入山澤，以漁獵為事。

translations.literal: He entered mountains and marshes and took fishing and hunting as his occupation.
translations.idiomatic: He roamed hills and wetlands and lived by fishing and the chase.

sentences.zh: 唯太原王乂謂舒曰：「卿終當為台輔，然今未能令妻子免饑寒，吾當助卿營之。

translations.literal: Only Wang Yi of Taiyuan said to Shu, “You will end as a pillar minister, yet now you cannot keep wife and children from cold and hunger; I shall help you arrange it.”
translations.idiomatic: Only Wang Yi of Taiyuan told him, “You are destined for the highest councils of state, but for now you cannot spare your family want; let me help you get on your feet.”

sentences.zh: 」常振其匱乏，舒受而不辭。

translations.literal: ” He often relieved his want; Shu accepted and did not decline.
translations.idiomatic: Wang regularly supplied him when he was short, and Shu accepted without false modesty.

sentences.zh: 舒嘗詣野王，主人妻夜產，俄而聞車馬之聲，相問曰：「男也，女也？

translations.literal: Shu once went to Yewang; the host’s wife gave birth by night; presently they heard the sound of carriage and horses, and asked one another, “Male or female?”
translations.idiomatic: On a visit to Yewang, Shu was there when the host’s wife delivered at night; soon voices outside—carriage and horses—called out, “Boy or girl?”

sentences.zh: 」曰：「男，書之，十五以兵死。

translations.literal: ” It was said, “Male; record it; at fifteen he will die by weapons.”
translations.idiomatic: The answer came: “A son. Mark it down—he will perish by arms at fifteen.”

sentences.zh: 」復問：「寢者為誰？

translations.literal: ” Again they asked, “Who is the sleeper?”
translations.idiomatic: They asked further, “Who is the guest asleep inside?”

sentences.zh: 」曰：「魏公舒。

translations.literal: ” It was said, “Lord Wei Shu.”
translations.idiomatic: “Wei Shu of Wei,” came the reply.

sentences.zh: 」後十五載，詣主人，問所生兒何在，曰：「因條桑為斧傷而死。

translations.literal: ” After fifteen years he went to the host and asked where the born child was; it was said, “Because of pruning mulberry he was wounded by an axe and died.”
translations.idiomatic: Fifteen years later he looked up the host and inquired after the child; he was told the boy had died from an axe cut while trimming mulberry—weapon enough to fulfill the omen.

sentences.zh: 」舒自知當為公矣。

translations.literal: ” Shu himself knew he would become a duke.
translations.idiomatic: Shu understood then that he was fated to rise to ducal rank.

sentences.zh: 年四十餘，郡上計掾察孝廉。

translations.literal: At over forty years, the commandery chief clerk for accounts recommended him as filial and incorrupt.
translations.idiomatic: Past forty, he was put forward as “filial and incorrupt” by the commandery’s accounts officer.

sentences.zh: 宗党以舒無學業，勸令不就，可以為高耳。

translations.literal: Clansmen and associates, because Shu had no scholarly learning, urged him not to take office, so as to be lofty.
translations.idiomatic: Kinsmen, knowing he had no classical training, urged him to stay home and preserve a reputation for high-minded refusal.

sentences.zh: 舒曰：「若試而不中，其負在我，安可虛竊不就之高以為己榮乎！

translations.literal: Shu said, “If I try and do not pass, the fault is mine; how can I vainly steal the loftiness of not going and make it my glory!”
translations.idiomatic: Shu objected: “If I sit the examination and fail, the blame is mine; I will not borrow the empty prestige of someone who never tried.”

sentences.zh: 」於是自課。

translations.literal: ” Thereupon he set himself lessons.
translations.idiomatic: He thereupon imposed a rigorous study regimen on himself.

sentences.zh: 百日習一經，因而對策升第。

translations.literal: In a hundred days he studied one classic, and thereby in the policy examination rose in rank.
translations.idiomatic: He mastered one classic every hundred days and passed the policy examination with a high placement.

sentences.zh: 除澠池長，遷浚儀令，入為尚書郎。

translations.literal: He was appointed magistrate of Mianchi, promoted to magistrate of Junyi, and entered as a Gentleman of the Masters of Writing.
translations.idiomatic: He was named magistrate of Mianchi, then of Junyi, and finally entered the capital as a secretary in the Masters of Writing.

sentences.zh: 時欲沙汰郎官。

translations.literal: At the time they wished to sift and dismiss Gentlemen.
translations.idiomatic: A purge of the Masters of Writing staff was underway.

sentences.zh: 非其才者罷之。

translations.literal: Those not of their talent were dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: Anyone judged incompetent was to be removed.

sentences.zh: 舒曰：「吾即其人也。

translations.literal: Shu said, “I am that person.”
translations.idiomatic: Shu said simply, “I am exactly the sort you mean to weed out.”

sentences.zh: 」襆被而出。

translations.literal: ” Bundling his bedding he went out.
translations.idiomatic: He rolled up his bedding and walked out on the spot.

sentences.zh: 同僚素無清論者咸有愧色，談者稱之。

translations.literal: Colleagues who ordinarily had no pure reputation all had ashamed expressions; discussers praised him.
translations.idiomatic: Coworkers who had never enjoyed a good name for integrity looked mortified, while observers praised his honesty.

sentences.zh: 累遷後將軍鐘毓長史，毓每與參佐射，舒常為畫籌而已。

translations.literal: He was promoted in stages to chief clerk to Rear General Zhong Yu; Yu whenever with aides shot archery, Shu always merely kept score with tallies.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to serve as chief clerk to Rear General Zhong Yu, who often held archery contests with his staff; Shu was usually relegated to keeping score.

sentences.zh: 後遇朋人不足，以舒滿數。

translations.literal: Later when companions were insufficient, they used Shu to fill the number.
translations.idiomatic: Once they were short a participant for the paired shooting, they drafted Shu to round out the party.

sentences.zh: 毓初不知其善射。

translations.literal: Yu at first did not know he was good at archery.
translations.idiomatic: Zhong Yu had no idea Shu could shoot.

sentences.zh: 舒容范閒雅，發無不中，舉坐愕然。

translations.literal: Shu’s deportment was leisurely and elegant; he released and none missed; the whole seated company was startled.
translations.idiomatic: Shu stepped up with unhurried grace and hit the mark every time, leaving the assembly dumbfounded.

sentences.zh: 莫有敵者。

translations.literal: There was none who matched him.
translations.idiomatic: No one there could rival him.

sentences.zh: 毓歎而謝曰：「吾之不足以盡卿才，有如此射矣，豈一事哉！

translations.literal: Yu sighed and apologized, saying, “My insufficiency to exhaust your talent is like this archery; is it only one matter!”
translations.idiomatic: Zhong Yu sighed and said, “If I have failed to use your abilities fully, this archery alone proves it— and that is hardly the only thing you can do!”

sentences.zh: 」轉相國參軍，封劇陽子。

translations.literal: ” He was transferred to aide to the minister of state and enfeoffed as Marquis of Juyang.
translations.idiomatic: He was reassigned as an adviser on the minister of state’s staff and enfeoffed as Marquis of Juyang.

sentences.zh: 府朝碎務，未嘗見是非；

translations.literal: In the bureau court on trivial affairs, he never showed right and wrong;
translations.idiomatic: On routine office business he never aired petty disputes;

sentences.zh: 至於廢興大事，眾人莫能斷者，舒徐為籌之，多出眾議之表。

translations.literal: as for rise-and-fall great matters that the multitude could not decide, Shu slowly planned them, often going beyond the surface of crowd discussion.
translations.idiomatic: but on weighty questions of state that stumped everyone, he would think them through quietly and usually see farther than the rest.

sentences.zh: 文帝深器重之，每朝會坐罷，目送之曰：「魏舒堂堂，人之領袖也。

translations.literal: Emperor Wen deeply valued him; every court assembly when sitting ended, watching him go with his eyes he said, “Wei Shu is imposing; he is the people’s leader.”
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wen thought the world of him; after each audience, as Shu withdrew, the emperor would watch him go and murmur, “Wei Shu has true stature—he is born to lead men.”

sentences.zh: 」遷宜陽、滎陽二郡太守，甚有聲稱。

translations.literal: ” He was promoted governor of the two commanderies Yiyang and Xingyang, and had very fine reputation.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed governor of both Yiyang and Xingyang and earned wide acclaim.

sentences.zh: 徵拜散騎常侍。

translations.literal: He was summoned and appointed Cavalier Attendant-in-Ordinary.
translations.idiomatic: He was recalled to court as a Cavalier Attendant-in-Ordinary.

sentences.zh: 出為冀州刺史，在州三年，以簡惠稱。

translations.literal: He went out as Inspector of Ji Province; in the province three years, he was praised for simplicity and kindness.
translations.idiomatic: He left the capital to serve as Inspector of Ji, where for three years he was known for a light touch and benevolent rule.

sentences.zh: 入為侍中。

translations.literal: He entered as Palace Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: He returned to the capital as a Palace Attendant.

sentences.zh: 武帝以舒清素，特賜絹百匹。

translations.literal: Emperor Wu, because Shu was pure and plain, specially gifted him one hundred bolts of silk.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu, honoring his austerity, presented him with a special grant of a hundred bolts of silk.

sentences.zh: 遷尚書，以公事當免官，詔以贖論。

translations.literal: He was promoted Master of Writing; because of public business he ought to have been dismissed from office; an edict judged it by ransom.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to Master of Writing; a bureaucratic infraction would normally have cost him his post, but the throne ruled the matter could be settled by a fine in lieu.

sentences.zh: 舒三娶妻皆亡，是歲自表乞假還本郡葬妻，詔賜葬地一頃，錢五十萬。

translations.literal: Shu thrice took wives and all died; that year he himself memorialized begging leave to return to his home commandery to bury his wife; an edict gifted burial land one qing and cash five hundred thousand.
translations.idiomatic: All three of Shu’s wives had predeceased him; that year he asked leave to go home and bury his latest spouse, and the court granted him a hectare of burial ground and half a million cash toward the funeral.

sentences.zh: 太康初，拜右僕射。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Taikang, he was appointed Right Vice Director.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Taikang era he was named Right Vice Director of the Masters of Writing.

sentences.zh: 舒與衛瓘、山濤、張華等以六合混一，宜用古典封禪東嶽，前後累陳其事，帝謙讓不許。

translations.literal: Shu with Wei Guan, Shan Tao, Zhang Hua, and others, because the six directions were unified, thought it fitting to use classical models to feng and shan the Eastern Marchmount; before and after they repeatedly presented this matter; the emperor modestly declined and did not permit.
translations.idiomatic: Shu joined Wei Guan, Shan Tao, Zhang Hua, and others in arguing that, with the realm reunited, the time had come for the classical Eastern Peak sacrifices of feng and shan; they pressed the case repeatedly, but the emperor demurred and refused.

sentences.zh: 以舒為左僕射，領吏部。

translations.literal: They appointed Shu Left Vice Director, heading the Ministry of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: Shu was made Left Vice Director of the Masters of Writing while concurrently directing appointments.

sentences.zh: 舒上言：「今選六宮，聘以玉帛，而舊使禦府丞奉聘，宣成嘉禮，贄重使輕。

translations.literal: Shu submitted words: “Now selecting the six palaces, betrothal is with jade and silks, yet the old practice sends the Masters of the Treasury aide to carry betrothal; proclaiming and completing the fine rite, the gifts are heavy and the envoy light.”
translations.idiomatic: Shu memorialized: “Selection for the harem is sealed with jade and silk, yet we still send a mere treasury aide as matchmaker; the gifts proclaim a grand rite, but the emissary’s rank belittles it.”

sentences.zh: 以為拜三夫人宜使卿，九嬪使五官中郎將，美人、良人使謁者，於典制為弘。

translations.literal: He thought investing the Three Ladies ought to use a minister, the Nine Concubines ought to use a Leader of Court Gentlemen for All Purposes, the Beauties and Good Women ought to use heralds; toward canonical regulations it would be ampler.
translations.idiomatic: He proposed that investitures for the Three Ladies be conducted by a minister, for the Nine Imperial Concubines by a Leader of Court Gentlemen for All Purposes, and for lower-ranking consorts by heralds—more in keeping with statutory dignity.”

sentences.zh: 」有詔詳之，眾議異同，遂寢。

translations.literal: ” There was an edict to examine it in detail; crowd discussion differed and agreed; thereupon it was shelved.
translations.idiomatic: The court ordered a review, but opinion split and the proposal died in committee.”

sentences.zh: 加右光祿大夫、儀同三司。

translations.literal: He was added Right Grand Master of Splendid Happiness, ceremonial equal to the Three Dukes.
translations.idiomatic: He was further honored as Right Grand Master of Splendid Happiness with ceremonial parity to the Three Dukes.

sentences.zh: 及山濤薨，以舒領司徒，有頃即真。

translations.literal: When Shan Tao died, they had Shu head the Minister of Education; after a short while he became substantive.
translations.idiomatic: On Shan Tao’s death Shu was placed in charge of the Ministry of Education and soon confirmed in full tenure.

sentences.zh: 舒有威重德望，祿賜散之九族，家無餘財。

translations.literal: Shu had awesome weight and virtuous reputation; salary gifts he scattered to the nine kin; the household had no surplus wealth.
translations.idiomatic: Shu combined moral authority with high prestige; he shared stipends and gifts across his extended family and kept nothing for himself.

sentences.zh: 陳留周震累為諸府所辟，辟書既下，公輒喪亡，僉號震為殺公掾，莫有辟者。

translations.literal: Zhou Zhen of Chenliu repeatedly was summoned by various bureaus; when the summons document had descended, the lord always died; all called Zhen “killer-of-lords clerk”; there was none who summoned.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Zhen of Chenliu had been recruited several times, but each time the appointment was issued the sponsoring minister died; people dubbed him the “death-bringing clerk,” and no one would hire him after that.

sentences.zh: 舒乃命之，而竟無患，識者以此稱其達命。

translations.literal: Shu thereupon ordered him, and in the end there was no calamity; knowers by this praised his comprehending fate.
translations.idiomatic: Shu nonetheless offered him a post, and no misfortune followed; observers cited this as proof of Shu’s grasp of destiny.

sentences.zh: 以年老，每稱疾遜位。

translations.literal: Because of old age, he often claimed illness and yielded position.
translations.idiomatic: As he aged he repeatedly pleaded illness to resign his offices.

sentences.zh: 中復暫起，署兗州中正，尋又稱疾。

translations.literal: In the midst again briefly he rose, was appointed Yan Province impartial judge, soon again claimed illness.
translations.idiomatic: He briefly returned to serve as provincial impartial judge for Yan, then once more retired on grounds of ill health.

sentences.zh: 尚書左丞郤詵與舒書曰：「公久疾小差，視事是也，唯上所念。

translations.literal: Xi Shen, Left Aide of the Masters of Writing, wrote Shu a letter saying, “Your lordship’s long illness has slightly improved; attending to affairs is right; only what superiors ponder.”
translations.idiomatic: Xi Shen, Left Aide of the Masters of Writing, wrote: “You have been unwell a long time but seem a little better; resuming duty would be fitting—that is what the throne expects.”

sentences.zh: 何竟起訖還臥，曲身回法，甚失具瞻之望。

translations.literal: Why in the end rise then finish and return to lie, bending body and turning law; very loses the hope of all who look.”
translations.idiomatic: Why appear at court only to go straight back to bed, dodging your responsibilities? It deeply disappoints everyone who looks to you.”

sentences.zh: 公少立巍巍，一旦棄之，可不惜哉！

translations.literal: Your lordship in youth established towering; once casting it away, can it not be pitiable!”
translations.idiomatic: You built a towering reputation in your prime—would you throw it away now? What a waste!”

sentences.zh: 」舒稱疾如初。

translations.literal: ” Shu claimed illness as at first.
translations.idiomatic: Shu continued to plead ill health as before.

sentences.zh: 後以災異遜位，帝不聽。

translations.literal: Later because of disasters and prodigies he yielded position; the emperor did not listen.
translations.idiomatic: He later cited ominous portents to resign, but the emperor would not hear of it.

sentences.zh: 後因正旦朝罷還第，表送章綬。

translations.literal: Later because of New Year’s Day court ending returning to mansion, he memorialized sending seals and ribbons.
translations.idiomatic: After the New Year audience he went home and formally returned his seals of office.

sentences.zh: 帝手詔敦勉。

translations.literal: The emperor by handwritten edict urged earnestly.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor answered with a personal edict urging him to stay.

sentences.zh: 而舒執意彌固，乃下詔曰：「司徒、劇陽子舒，體道弘粹，思量經遠，忠肅居正，在公盡規。

translations.literal: But Shu’s held intention was more firm; thereupon an edict was issued saying, “Minister of Education, Marquis of Juyang Shu, embodies the Way in great purity, thought and measure reach far, loyal and solemn dwelling in rectitude, in public exhausting regulation.”
translations.idiomatic: Shu would not budge, so the throne issued an edict: “Minister of Education and Marquis of Juyang Wei Shu embodies the Way in its purest breadth, plans with long vision, serves with loyal dignity, and gives the state his utmost counsel.”

sentences.zh: 入管銓衡，官人允敘；

translations.literal: Entering he managed balance-weights; officials and men were duly ordered;
translations.idiomatic: Within the ministry he set the standard for appointments and saw men placed in proper order;

sentences.zh: 出贊袞職，敷弘五教。

translations.literal: going out he assisted the ducal office, spread and enlarged the five teachings.
translations.idiomatic: in the outer administration he supported the ducal councils and spread the five moral teachings.”

sentences.zh: 惠訓播流，德聲茂著，可謂朝之俊乂者也。

translations.literal: Kind instruction broadcast and flowed; virtuous fame luxuriantly manifest; can be called the court’s outstanding talent.”
translations.idiomatic: His gentle guidance has reached everywhere, and his virtuous name shines brightly—truly he is one of the court’s foremost men.”

sentences.zh: 而屢執沖讓，辭旨懇誠，申覽反覆，省用憮然。

translations.literal: Yet repeatedly he holds modest yielding; words and intent are earnest and sincere; extending and viewing repeatedly, examining use is sorrowful.”
translations.idiomatic: Yet he has repeatedly pressed his modest wish to retire; his petitions are heartfelt, and each time We read them through We are moved with regret.”

sentences.zh: 蓋成人之美，先典所與，難違至情。

translations.literal: For completing others’ beauty, what former canons grant, hard to oppose utmost feeling.”
translations.idiomatic: The classics teach Us to honor another’s noble purpose, and We cannot deny so sincere a plea.”

sentences.zh: 今聽其所執，以劇陽子就第，位同三司，祿賜如前。

translations.literal: Now We listen to what he holds; as Marquis of Juyang go to mansion; position equal Three Dukes; salary gifts as before.”
translations.idiomatic: We therefore grant his wish: he may retire to private life as Marquis of Juyang with rank equal to the Three Dukes and keep his former stipends and perquisites.”

sentences.zh: 几杖不朝，賜錢百萬，床帳簟褥自副。

translations.literal: With stool and staff not attend court; gift cash one million; bed curtains and bamboo mats and bedding self-provided as adjunct.”
translations.idiomatic: He need not attend court; We grant a million cash and supply bed hangings, mats, and bedding for his household.”

sentences.zh: 以舍人四人為劇陽子舍人，置官騎十人。

translations.literal: With four Gentlemen-in-Attendance as Marquis of Juyang Gentlemen; establish official riders ten men.”
translations.idiomatic: Four Gentlemen-in-Attendance shall attend the marquis, and ten mounted guards shall be assigned to him.”

sentences.zh: 使光祿勳奉策，主者詳案典禮，令皆如舊制。

translations.literal: Order the Minister of the Imperial Clan to present the document; those in charge examine in detail canonical rites; command all as old regulations.”
translations.idiomatic: The Minister of the Imperial Clan shall convey the patent; responsible offices shall follow precedent in every ceremonial detail.”

sentences.zh: 」於是賜安車駟馬，門施行馬。

translations.literal: ” Thereupon gifted secure carriage four-horse team; at gate erecting riding-horses barrier.”
translations.idiomatic: He was also given a comfortable carriage with a four-horse team and the right to mount crossbars at his gate.”

sentences.zh: 舒為事必先行而後言，遜位之際，莫有知者。

translations.literal: Shu in doing matters always first acted then spoke; at the juncture of yielding position, there was none who knew.
translations.idiomatic: Shu always acted before he spoke; when he stepped down, no one had seen it coming.

sentences.zh: 時論以為晉興以來，三公能辭榮善終者，未之有也。

translations.literal: Contemporary opinion thought since Jin rose, among the Three Dukes able to decline glory and end well, there had not been such.
translations.idiomatic: Opinion held that since the Jin dynasty began, no one among the Three Dukes had relinquished power so gracefully and died in honor—until Shu.

sentences.zh: 司空衛瓘與舒書曰：「每與足下共論此事，日日未果，可謂瞻之在前，忽焉在後矣。

translations.literal: Minister of Works Wei Guan wrote Shu a letter saying, “Whenever with you I together discuss this matter, day by day not yet fruit; can be called ‘it seems before the eyes, suddenly it is behind.’”
translations.idiomatic: Minister of Works Wei Guan wrote: “We spoke of this again and again, yet never pinned it down—like something right in front of you that slips away the moment you grasp for it.”

sentences.zh: 」太熙元年薨，時年八十二。

translations.literal: ” In the first year of Taixi he died; at the time age eighty-two.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the first year of Taixi, aged eighty-two.

sentences.zh: 帝甚傷悼，賵賻優厚，諡曰康。

translations.literal: The emperor greatly mourned; funeral gifts were generous; posthumous name was Kang.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor grieved deeply, sent lavish funeral goods, and gave him the posthumous title “Kang” (“Peaceful”).

sentences.zh: 子混，字延廣，清惠有才行，為太子舍人。

translations.literal: Son Hun, courtesy name Yanguang, pure and kind had talent and conduct, was Crown Prince attendant.
translations.idiomatic: His son Hun, courtesy name Yanguang, was clear-minded, generous, and able, and served as an attendant to the heir apparent.

sentences.zh: 年二十七，先舒卒，朝野咸為舒悲惜。

translations.literal: Age twenty-seven, before Shu died; court and wild all for Shu grieved and pitied.
translations.idiomatic: He died at twenty-seven, predeceasing his father; officials and commoners alike mourned for Shu.

sentences.zh: 舒每哀慟，退而歎曰：「吾不及莊生遠矣，豈以無益自損乎！

translations.literal: Shu every time mourned in grief; retiring sighed saying, “I do not reach Master Zhuang by far; how by what is without benefit self-harm!”
translations.idiomatic: Shu grieved bitterly, then sighed, “I am no Zhuangzi; why harm myself with useless sorrow?”

sentences.zh: 」於是終服不復哭。

translations.literal: ” Thereupon to the end of mourning did not again weep.
translations.idiomatic: For the rest of the mourning period he did not weep again.

sentences.zh: 詔曰：「舒惟一子，薄命短折。

translations.literal: An edict said, “Shu has only one son; thin fate short broken.”
translations.idiomatic: An edict read: “Shu had but one son, and fate cut him off in youth.”

sentences.zh: 舒告老之年，處窮獨之苦，每念怛然，為之嗟悼。

translations.literal: Shu in years of announcing old, dwells in destitute alone’s bitterness; every thought is startled; for it sighs in grief.”
translations.idiomatic: In the years when Shu has begged to retire he endures the loneliness of a bereaved old man; the thought wrings Our heart.”

sentences.zh: 思所以散愁養氣，可更增滋味品物。

translations.literal: Think that whereby scatter sorrow nurture breath; can further increase flavors and kinds of things.”
translations.idiomatic: We would ease his sorrow and restore his spirits—let richer fare and comforts be added to his table.”

sentences.zh: 仍給賜陽燧四望繐窗戶皁輪車牛一乘，庶出入觀望，或足散憂也。

translations.literal: Still grant a yang-sui four-view fringe-window black-wheeled carriage ox one team; perhaps going out and in looking about, perhaps suffices to scatter sorrow.”
translations.idiomatic: Grant him besides a sun-canopied four-window carriage with black wheels and a team of oxen, so drives about the city may lift his gloom.”

sentences.zh: 」以庶孫融嗣。

translations.literal: ” With grandson by concubine Rong succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: His grandson Rong, born of a concubine’s line, was named heir.

sentences.zh: 又早卒，從孫晃嗣。

translations.literal: Again early died; great-grandson Huang succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: Rong also died young, and the succession passed to a great-grandson, Huang.

sentences.zh: 李憙，字季和，上黨銅鞮人也。

translations.literal: Li Xi, courtesy name Jihe, was a man of Tongdi in Shangdang.
translations.idiomatic: Li Xi, whose courtesy name was Jihe, came from Tongdi in Shangdang commandery.

sentences.zh: 父牷，漢大鴻臚。

translations.literal: Father Quan, Han Grand Herald.
translations.idiomatic: His father Quan had been Grand Herald under the Han.

sentences.zh: 憙少有高行，博學研精，與北海管甯以賢良征，不行。

translations.literal: Xi in youth had high conduct, broad learning and refined study; with Guan Ning of Beihai by worthy and good was summoned; did not go.
translations.idiomatic: From youth Xi showed sterling character and wide, meticulous scholarship; he and Guan Ning of Beihai were summoned as “worthy and good” candidates, but he declined to report.

sentences.zh: 累辟三府，不就。

translations.literal: Repeatedly summoned by Three Offices; did not take office.
translations.idiomatic: The Three Ducal Offices summoned him repeatedly; each time he refused.

sentences.zh: 宣帝復辟憙為太傅屬，固辭疾，郡縣扶輿上道，時憙母疾篤，乃竊逾泫氏城而徒還，遂遭母喪，論者嘉其志節。

translations.literal: Emperor Xuan again summoned Xi as Grand Tutor subordinate; firmly declined illness; commandery and county supported carriage onto road; at the time Xi’s mother was gravely ill; thereupon secretly crossed Xuanshi city and on foot returned; thereupon suffered mother mourning; discussers praised his will and integrity.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xuan appointed him to the Grand Tutor’s staff; he pleaded illness, but local officials forced him into a litter for the journey. His mother lay dying, so he slipped away, slipped past Xuanshi, and walked home; she died soon after, and commentators honored his devotion.

sentences.zh: 後為并州別駕，時驍騎將軍秦朗過并州，州將畢軌敬焉。

translations.literal: Later he became Bing Province aide; at the time Valiant Cavalry General Qin Lang passed Bing Province; the province general Bi Gui respected him.
translations.idiomatic: He later served as senior aide in Bing Province when Valiant Cavalry General Qin Lang passed through; the provincial commander Bi Gui treated him with marked respect.

sentences.zh: 令乘車至閣。

translations.literal: He ordered him to ride in a carriage to the gate tower.
translations.idiomatic: He insisted that Xi ride in a carriage right up to the gate pavilion.

sentences.zh: 憙固諫以為不可，軌不得已從之。

translations.literal: Xi firmly remonstrated, deeming it impermissible; Gui had no choice but to follow him.
translations.idiomatic: Xi protested firmly that this was improper, and Bi Gui had no choice but yield.

sentences.zh: 景帝輔政，命憙為大將軍從事中郎，憙到，引見，謂憙曰：「昔先公辟君而君不應，今孤命君而君至，何也？

translations.literal: Emperor Jing assisted governance, ordered Xi as Colonel in the Army of the Grand General; Xi arrived, was led in audience, and was told Xi, “Formerly my late father summoned you and you did not respond; now I order you and you have come—why?”
translations.idiomatic: While Emperor Jing was regent, he named Xi a staff colonel on the grand general’s command. When Xi reported for duty and was received in audience, the regent asked, “My father once called you to office and you stayed away; I summon you and you come—how is that?”

sentences.zh: 」對曰：「先君以禮見待，憙得以禮進退。

translations.literal: ” He replied, “The late lord treated me with ritual; Xi was able by ritual to advance or withdraw.”
translations.idiomatic: Xi answered, “Your father received me according to propriety, so I could accept or decline in kind.”

sentences.zh: 明公以法見繩，憙畏法而至。

translations.literal: The enlightened lord by law sees binding; Xi fears law and therefore came.”
translations.idiomatic: Your lordship rules by law; I obeyed the law and came.”

sentences.zh: 」帝甚重之。

translations.literal: ” The emperor greatly esteemed him.
translations.idiomatic: The regent thought highly of him.

sentences.zh: 轉司馬，尋拜右長史。

translations.literal: He was transferred to marshal, soon appointed Right Chief Clerk.
translations.idiomatic: He was reassigned as marshal, then soon named Right Chief Clerk.

sentences.zh: 從討毌丘儉還，遷御史中丞。

translations.literal: Following the campaign against Guanqiu Jian and returning, he was promoted Palace Assistant Secretary.
translations.idiomatic: After the expedition against Guanqiu Jian he was promoted to Palace Assistant Secretary.

sentences.zh: 當官正色，不憚強禦，百僚震肅焉。

translations.literal: Holding office with stern countenance, he did not fear the powerful; the hundred officials were awed and solemn.
translations.idiomatic: In office he was fearless before the mighty, and the whole bureaucracy stood in awe.

sentences.zh: 薦樂安孫璞，亦以道德顯，時人稱為知人。

translations.literal: He recommended Sun Pu of Le’an, who also by virtue and the Way was eminent; people of the time called him one who knew men.
translations.idiomatic: He recommended Sun Pu of Le’an, another man of moral stature, and contemporaries praised his eye for talent.

sentences.zh: 尋遷大司馬，以公事免。

translations.literal: Soon he was promoted Grand Marshal, and because of public business was dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon raised to Grand Marshal, then removed over an administrative matter.

sentences.zh: 司馬伷為甯北將軍，鎮鄴，以憙為軍司。

translations.literal: Sima Zhou was General Who Pacifies the North, garrisoned Ye, and appointed Xi army director.
translations.idiomatic: When Sima Zhou held Ye as General Who Pacifies the North, he named Xi director of his headquarters.

sentences.zh: 頃之，除涼州刺史，加揚威將軍、假節，領護羌校尉，綏禦華夷，甚有聲績。

translations.literal: Presently he was appointed Inspector of Liang, added General Who Displays Might, credential staff, heading Colonel Protecting the Qiang, pacifying and controlling Chinese and barbarians, had very fine reputation and achievement.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he became Inspector of Liang with the added titles General Who Displays Might and acting Colonel Protecting the Qiang, staff of authority in hand; he kept peace among Han and non-Han peoples and earned a strong record.

sentences.zh: 羌虜犯塞，憙因其隙會，不及啟聞，輒以便宜出軍深入，遂大克獲，以功重免譴，時人比之漢朝馮、甘焉。

translations.literal: Qiang raiders violated the passes; Xi because of their gap opportunity, before reaching memorial and hearing, then on expedient authority sent the army deep in, thereupon greatly conquered and captured; by merit weight was exempted reproach; people of the time compared him to Han dynasty Feng and Gan.
translations.idiomatic: When Qiang raiders struck the frontier, Xi seized the opening before he could seek court approval, ordered troops forward on his own authority, and won a major victory; his success outweighed any charge of overstepping, and observers likened him to Feng Fengshi and Gan Yanshou of the Han.

sentences.zh: 於是請還，許之。

translations.literal: Thereupon he requested return; it was permitted.
translations.idiomatic: He asked to come home, and the court agreed.

sentences.zh: 居家月餘，拜冀州刺史，累遷司隸校尉。

translations.literal: Dwelling at home over a month, he was appointed Inspector of Ji, promoted in stages to Metropolitan Commandant.
translations.idiomatic: After a month at home he was named Inspector of Ji and eventually rose to Metropolitan Commandant.

sentences.zh: 及魏帝告禪于晉，憙以本官行司徒事，副太尉鄭沖奉策。

translations.literal: When the Wei emperor announced abdication to Jin, Xi by his original office acted Minister of Education affairs, assisting Grand Commandant Zheng Chong in presenting the document.
translations.idiomatic: When the Wei emperor abdicated in favor of Jin, Xi served provisionally as Minister of Education while assisting Grand Commandant Zheng Chong in presenting the patent of succession.

sentences.zh: 泰始初，封祁侯。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Taishi, he was enfeoffed Marquis of Qi.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Taishi he was enfeoffed as Marquis of Qi.

sentences.zh: 憙上言：「故立進令劉友、前尚書山濤、中山王睦、故尚書僕射武陔各占官三更稻田，請免濤、睦等官。

translations.literal: Xi submitted words: “Former Lijin magistrate Liu You, former Master of Writing Shan Tao, Prince Mu of Zhongshan, former Vice Director of the Masters of Writing Wu Gai each occupied government three-commandery paddy fields; request dismissal of Tao, Mu, and others from office.”
translations.idiomatic: Xi memorialized that the former magistrate of Lijin Liu You, the former Master of Writing Shan Tao, Prince Mu of Zhongshan, and the late Vice Director Wu Gai had each seized government rice land across three commanderies, and he asked that Shan Tao, the prince, and their ilk be stripped of office.”

sentences.zh: 陔已亡，請貶諡。

translations.literal: Gai already died; request degrading posthumous name.”
translations.idiomatic: Wu Gai was already dead; Xi asked that his posthumous title be reduced.”

sentences.zh: 」詔曰：「法者，天下取正，不避親貴，然後行耳，吾豈將枉縱其間哉！

translations.literal: ” An edict said, “Law is what the realm takes as correct; not avoiding kin and nobles, afterward it is enacted—how could I intend to bend and indulge therein!”
translations.idiomatic: The throne replied: “The law must be the standard for all, kin and grandees included; I will not twist it for anyone’s convenience.”

sentences.zh: 然案此事皆是友所作，侵剝百姓，以繆惑朝士。

translations.literal: Yet examining this matter, it was all You who did it, encroaching and stripping the hundred surnames, thereby falsely deluding court gentlemen.
translations.idiomatic: The inquiry shows Liu You alone engineered the seizures, fleecing the people and misleading officials at court.

sentences.zh: 奸吏乃敢作此，其考竟友以懲邪佞。

translations.literal: Wicked clerks then dared do this; investigate to the end You to punish wicked flattery.
translations.idiomatic: Corrupt underlings dared this; try Liu You to the full extent of the law as a warning to sycophants.”

sentences.zh: 濤等不貳其過者，皆勿有所問。

translations.literal: Tao and others who did not double their faults, all do not have anything questioned.
translations.idiomatic: Shan Tao and the rest, having no second offense, shall face no further inquiry.”

sentences.zh: 《易》稱'王臣蹇蹇，匪躬之故'。

translations.literal: The Changes says, ‘The king’s minister is in straits, straits—not for his own body’s cause.’”
translations.idiomatic: As the Book of Changes puts it, ‘The king’s minister suffers hardship—not for private gain.’”

sentences.zh: 今憙亢志在公，當官而行，可謂'邦之司直'者矣。

translations.literal: Now Xi high-minded will is in public, holding office and acting; can be called ‘the state’s straightener.’”
translations.idiomatic: Li Xi serves the public good without flinching; he is truly what the ode calls ‘the straightener of the state.’”

sentences.zh: 光武有云：'貴戚且斂手以避二鮑'。

translations.literal: Emperor Guangwu had words: ‘Noble kin moreover fold hands to avoid the two Baos.’”
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Guangwu said that even imperial in-laws kept their hands folded to stay clear of Bao Yong and Bao Xian.”

sentences.zh: 豈其然乎！

translations.literal: How could it be thus!”
translations.idiomatic: Should it not be so today?”

sentences.zh: 其申敕群僚，各慎所司，寬宥之恩，不可數遇也。

translations.literal: Command the host of officials, each careful in what they administer; lenient pardon’s grace cannot be repeatedly encountered.”
translations.idiomatic: Let every official mind his charge—imperial mercy is not something you can count on twice.”

sentences.zh: 」憙為二代司隸，朝野稱之。

translations.literal: ” Xi was Metropolitan Commandant for two reigns; court and wild praised him.
translations.idiomatic: Xi served two reigns as Metropolitan Commandant and won praise in court and countryside alike.

sentences.zh: 以公事免。

translations.literal: Because of public business he was dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: He was removed from office over an administrative matter.

sentences.zh: 其年，皇太子立，以憙為太子太傅。

translations.literal: That year the crown prince was established; Xi was appointed Grand Tutor to the crown prince.
translations.idiomatic: The same year the heir apparent was invested, Xi became his Grand Tutor.

sentences.zh: 自魏明帝以後，久曠東宮，制度廢闕，官司不具，詹事、左右率、庶子、中舍人諸官並未置，唯置衛率令典兵，二傅並攝眾事。

translations.literal: From Wei Emperor Ming afterward, long the Eastern Palace was vacant; regulations abandoned and lacking, offices not complete; Household Superintendent, Left and Right Rates, Mentors, Gentlemen Attendants within the Household various offices all not yet established; only was established Guard Rate commander commanding troops; the two tutors together administered crowd matters.
translations.idiomatic: Since Emperor Ming of Wei the heir’s quarters had stood empty; institutions had lapsed, posts were unfilled, and offices such as the Household Superintendent, the Left and Right Guard Leaders, the Mentors, and the Gentlemen Attendants did not exist—only a Guard commander held troops, while both tutors handled every other duty.

sentences.zh: 憙在位累年，訓道盡規。

translations.literal: Xi in position accumulated years, instruction and guidance exhausted regulation.
translations.idiomatic: Xi held the post for years, teaching the heir and offering unstinting counsel.

sentences.zh: 遷尚書僕射，拜特進、光祿大夫，以年老遜位。

translations.literal: He was promoted Vice Director of the Masters of Writing, appointed Specially Advanced, Grand Master of Splendid Happiness, because of old age yielded position.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to Vice Director of the Masters of Writing and received the titles Specially Advanced and Grand Master of Splendid Happiness, then retired on account of age.

sentences.zh: 詔曰：「光祿大夫、特進李憙，杖德居義，當升台司。

translations.literal: An edict said, “Grand Master of Splendid Happiness, Specially Advanced Li Xi, leaning on virtue dwelling in righteousness, ought to ascend terrace office.”
translations.idiomatic: An edict read: “Grand Master of Splendid Happiness and Specially Advanced Li Xi, a pillar of virtue and integrity, was fit for the highest councils.”

sentences.zh: 毗亮朕躬，而以年尊致仕。

translations.literal: He assisted and brightened Our person, yet by age honor retired office.”
translations.idiomatic: He aided and enlightened Us, yet chose to retire on grounds of age.”

sentences.zh: 雖優遊無為，可以頤神，而虛心之望，能不憮然！

translations.literal: Although leisurely without action can nurture spirit, yet empty-heart’s hope—can one not be sorrowful!”
translations.idiomatic: Leisure may nourish the spirit, yet how can We not feel the ache of an unfulfilled hope!”

sentences.zh: 其因光祿之號，改假金紫，置官騎十人，賜錢五十萬，祿賜班禮，一如三司，門施行馬。」

translations.literal: Let him by Grand Master of Splendid Happiness’s title, change to lent gold and purple, establish official riders ten men, gift cash five hundred thousand; salary gifts and court ritual, all as Three Dukes; at gate erect riding-horses barrier.”
translations.idiomatic: Retain his Splendid Happiness title but grant gold ribbon and purple sash, assign ten mounted attendants, and award half a million cash; his stipends and court precedence shall match the Three Dukes, with crossbars mounted at his gate.”

sentences.zh: 初，憙為僕射時，涼州虜寇邊，憙唱義遣軍討之。

translations.literal: At first, when Xi was Vice Director, Liang Province barbarians raided the border; Xi raised righteousness and sent army to punish them.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, while Xi was Vice Director, tribes on the Liang frontier raided the border; he was the first to urge a punitive expedition.

sentences.zh: 朝士謂出兵不易，虜未足為患，竟不從之。

translations.literal: Court gentlemen said sending troops was not easy, barbarians not sufficient to be trouble; in the end did not follow him.
translations.idiomatic: Courtiers argued that mobilizing troops was too costly and the raiders no real threat, and in the end they ignored him.

sentences.zh: 後虜果大縱逸，涼州覆沒，朝廷深悔焉。

translations.literal: Later barbarians indeed greatly ran rampant; Liang Province overturned and drowned; the court deeply regretted it.
translations.idiomatic: The tribes then ran wild, Liang fell, and the court bitterly regretted its refusal.

sentences.zh: 以憙清素貧儉，賜絹百匹。

translations.literal: Because Xi was pure, plain, poor, and frugal, gifted one hundred bolts of silk.
translations.idiomatic: Because he lived in austere poverty, the court granted him a hundred bolts of silk.

sentences.zh: 及齊王攸出鎮，憙上疏諫爭，辭甚懇切。

translations.literal: When Prince You of Qi went out to garrison, Xi submitted memorial remonstrating and contending; words were very earnest and cutting.
translations.idiomatic: When Prince You of Qi was sent to his princely fief, Xi submitted a passionate memorial of protest.

sentences.zh: 憙自曆仕，雖清非異眾，而家無儲積，親舊故人乃至分衣共食，未嘗私以王官。

translations.literal: Xi from accumulated service, although pure was not different from the multitude, yet the household had no stored accumulation; kin, old, and former friends even divided clothes and shared food; never privately used kingly office.
translations.idiomatic: Through a long career he remained no richer than most honest men—there was nothing laid by, and he shared clothes and food with friends and kin—yet he never abused public office for private gain.

sentences.zh: 及卒，追贈太保，諡曰成。

translations.literal: When he died, posthumously gifted Grand Guardian, posthumous name Cheng.
translations.idiomatic: After his death he was posthumously honored as Grand Guardian with the title “Cheng” (“Accomplished”).

sentences.zh: 子贊嗣。

translations.literal: Son Zan succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: His son Zan inherited the title.

sentences.zh: 少子儉，字仲約，曆左積弩將軍、屯騎校尉。

translations.literal: Younger son Jian, courtesy name Zhongyue, passed through General of the Left Crossbowmen, Colonel of Garrison Cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: His younger son Jian, courtesy name Zhongyue, served as General of the Left Crossbowmen and Colonel of Garrison Cavalry.

sentences.zh: 儉子弘，字世彥，少有清節，永嘉末，曆給事黃門侍郎、散騎常侍。

translations.literal: Jian’s son Hong, courtesy name Shiyan, in youth had pure integrity; at the end of Yongjia, passed through Palace Attendant within the Yellow Gates, Cavalier Attendant-in-Ordinary.
translations.idiomatic: Jian’s son Hong, courtesy name Shiyan, was known in youth for integrity; late in Yongjia he held the posts of Palace Attendant within the Yellow Gates and Cavalier Attendant-in-Ordinary.

sentences.zh: 劉寔，字子真，平原高唐人也。

translations.literal: Liu Shi, courtesy name Zizhen, was a man of Gaotang in Pingyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Shi, courtesy name Zizhen, was a native of Gaotang in Pingyuan commandery.

sentences.zh: 漢濟北惠王壽之後也，父廣，斥丘令。

translations.literal: He was a descendant of Han Prince Hui of Jibei, Shou; father Guang, magistrate of Chiqiu.
translations.idiomatic: He descended from Prince Hui of Jibei, Liu Shou, of the Han; his father Guang had been magistrate of Chiqiu.

sentences.zh: 寔少貧苦，賣牛衣以自給。

translations.literal: Shi in youth was poor and bitter, sold cattle blankets to supply himself.
translations.idiomatic: He grew up in grinding poverty and sold straw cattle-mats to get by.

sentences.zh: 然好學，手約繩，口誦書，博通古今。

translations.literal: Yet he loved learning, hand bound rope, mouth recited books, broadly penetrated ancient and modern.
translations.idiomatic: Yet he loved books, knotted cords on his wrist as prompts, recited texts aloud, and mastered the classical tradition from antiquity to his own day.

sentences.zh: 清身潔己，行無瑕玷。

translations.literal: He purified body and cleansed self; conduct had no flaw-stain.
translations.idiomatic: He kept himself scrupulously clean and his conduct without blemish.

sentences.zh: 郡察孝廉，州舉秀才，皆不行。

translations.literal: The commandery investigated him as filial and incorrupt; the province raised him as flourishing talent; all he did not go.
translations.idiomatic: The commandery nominated him as filial and incorrupt and the province as a “flourishing talent”; he declined both.

sentences.zh: 以計吏入洛，調為河南尹丞，遷尚書郎、廷尉正。

translations.literal: As accounts clerk he entered Luoyang, was transferred to aide to the Governor of Henan, promoted Gentleman of the Masters of Writing, Director of Justice rectifier.
translations.idiomatic: He went to Luoyang as a commandery accounts officer, was named aide to the Governor of Henan, and rose to secretary in the Masters of Writing and senior judge in the court of justice.

sentences.zh: 後曆吏部郎，參文帝相國軍事，封循陽子。

translations.literal: Later he passed through Gentleman of the Ministry of Personnel, participated in Emperor Wen’s minister of state military affairs, enfeoffed Marquis of Xunyang.
translations.idiomatic: He later served in the Ministry of Personnel, joined the staff of Sima Zhao as minister of state, and was enfeoffed as Marquis of Xunyang.

sentences.zh: 鐘會、鄧艾之伐蜀也，有客問寔曰：「二將其平蜀乎？

translations.literal: When Zhong Hui and Deng Ai campaigned against Shu, a guest asked Shi, “Will the two generals pacify Shu?”
translations.idiomatic: During Zhong Hui and Deng Ai’s invasion of Shu, a visitor asked Liu Shi whether the two generals would conquer the riverlands.

sentences.zh: 」寔曰：「破蜀必矣，而皆不還。

translations.literal: ” Shi said, “Destroying Shu is certain, yet both will not return.”
translations.idiomatic: Shi answered, “They will crush Shu, but neither will come back alive.”

sentences.zh: 」客問其故，笑而不答，竟如其言。

translations.literal: ” The guest asked the reason; he smiled and did not answer; in the end it was as his words.
translations.idiomatic: When pressed for an explanation he smiled and said nothing; events proved him right.

sentences.zh: 寔之先見，皆此類也。

translations.literal: Shi’s foresight was all of this kind.
translations.idiomatic: His prescience was often of this sort.

sentences.zh: 以世多進趣，廉遜道闕，乃著《崇讓論》以矯之。

translations.literal: Because the age had much advancing ambition, the way of integrity and yielding lacked, thereupon he composed “Treatise Exalting Yielding” to correct it.
translations.idiomatic: Seeing his contemporaries scramble for advancement while modesty vanished, he wrote “On Exalting Yielding” to set matters right.

sentences.zh: 其辭曰：

translations.literal: Its words say:
translations.idiomatic: It begins:

sentences.zh: 古之聖王之化天下，所以貴讓者，欲以出賢才，息爭競也。

translations.literal: The ancient sage kings’ transforming the realm, the reason they esteemed yielding was desiring thereby to bring forth worthy talent, rest striving and competing.
translations.idiomatic: The sage-kings of old prized yielding because it brought worthy men forward and stilled destructive rivalry.

sentences.zh: 夫人情莫不欲已之賢也，故勸令讓賢以自明賢也，豈假讓不賢哉！

translations.literal: As for human feeling none does not desire self’s worthiness; therefore urge ordering yield worthies to self-clarify worthiness; how borrow yielding not worthy!”
translations.idiomatic: Everyone wishes to be thought worthy, so we urge them to yield place to the better qualified and thus prove their own quality—this is no pretense of yielding to the unworthy!”

sentences.zh: 故讓道興，賢能之人不求而自出矣，至公之舉自立矣，百官之副亦豫具矣。

translations.literal: Therefore yielding way rises, worthy able men not sought and self emerge; utmost impartial selection self stands; hundred officials’ deputies also beforehand are provided.
translations.idiomatic: When yielding prevails, able men step forward unbidden, the most impartial choices make themselves, and deputy posts are filled in advance.

sentences.zh: 一官缺，擇眾官所讓最多者而用之，審之道也。

translations.literal: One office vacant, select among the host of officials the one yielded to most and use him; this is the way of carefulness.
translations.idiomatic: When a post opens, appoint the man most often yielded to by his peers—that is sound policy.

sentences.zh: 在朝之士相讓於上，草廬之人咸皆化之，推賢讓能之風從此生矣。

translations.literal: Gentlemen at court yield to one another upward; thatched-hut people all are transformed by it; pushing worthies and yielding ability’s wind from this is born.
translations.idiomatic: If ministers defer to one another before the throne, commoners in their huts will follow suit, and a culture of recommending the able will take root.

sentences.zh: 為一國所讓，則一國士也；

translations.literal: By one state yielded to, then one state’s gentleman;
translations.idiomatic: The man an entire kingdom would yield to is that kingdom’s foremost gentleman;

sentences.zh: 天下所共推，則天下士也。

translations.literal: what the realm together pushes, then is the realm’s gentleman.
translations.idiomatic: the man the whole realm would advance is the foremost gentleman of the age.

sentences.zh: 推讓之風行，則賢與不肖灼然殊矣。

translations.literal: Pushing-yielding’s wind practiced, then worthy and unworthy burningly differ.
translations.idiomatic: Once yielding is the fashion, worthy and unworthy stand clearly apart.

sentences.zh: 此道之行，在上者無所用其心，因成清議，隨之而已。

translations.literal: This way’s practice, those above have nothing to use their hearts on; thereby pure discussion forms; following it only.
translations.idiomatic: Under such a system rulers need not micromanage; pure public opinion does the sorting for them.

sentences.zh: 故曰，蕩蕩乎堯之為君，莫之能名。

translations.literal: Therefore it is said, vast vast! Yao’s being lord—none can name it.
translations.idiomatic: Hence the saying: “How vast was Yao as ruler—no one could put a name to his art.”

sentences.zh: 言天下自安矣，不見堯所以化之，故不能名也。

translations.literal: It means the realm self was at peace; not seeing Yao’s means of transforming it, therefore could not name it.
translations.idiomatic: The realm was at peace of itself; people could not point to how Yao had engineered it, and so could not describe his method.

sentences.zh: 又曰，舜禹之有天下而不與焉，無為而化者其舜也歟。

translations.literal: Again it is said, Shun and Yu’s having the realm yet not participating therein—without action yet transforming: is it Shun!”
translations.idiomatic: It is also said that Shun and Yu possessed the realm as if it were not theirs—who ruled by nonaction if not Shun?”

sentences.zh: 賢人相讓于朝，大才之人恆在大官，小人不爭於野，天下無事矣。

translations.literal: Worthy men yield to one another at court; great talent men always are in great offices; petty men do not contend in the wilds; the realm has no affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Let worthies defer in court, place great talent in high office, and keep petty strivers from the countryside, and the realm will know no turmoil.

sentences.zh: 以賢才化無事，至道興矣。

translations.literal: By worthy talent transform to no affairs; utmost Way rises.
translations.idiomatic: Governing through worthy men until nothing remains to do is the highest Way.

sentences.zh: 已仰其成，復何與焉！

translations.literal: Already relying on its completion, again what participation therein!
translations.idiomatic: The ruler has only to trust the outcome—what need is there to meddle?”

sentences.zh: 故可以歌《南風》之詩，彈五弦之琴也。

translations.literal: Therefore can sing “South Wind” poem, pluck five-stringed zither.
translations.idiomatic: Then he may sing the “South Wind” and strum the five-string lute in peace.

sentences.zh: 成此功者非有他，崇讓之所致耳。

translations.literal: Completing this achievement has nothing else; exalting yielding’s what brought it only.
translations.idiomatic: No other art produced such order—only the exaltation of yielding.

sentences.zh: 孔子曰，能以禮讓為國，則不難也。

translations.literal: Confucius said, able to take ritual yielding as state, then it is not difficult.
translations.idiomatic: Confucius said that ruling a state through courteous yielding presents no difficulty.

sentences.zh: 在朝之人不務相讓久矣，天下化之。

translations.literal: Those at court long have not endeavored mutual yielding; the realm was transformed by it.
translations.idiomatic: Courtiers have long ceased to defer to one another, and the whole realm has taken its cue from them.

sentences.zh: 自魏代以來，登進辟命之士，及在職之吏，臨見受敘，雖自辭不能，終莫肯讓有勝己者。

translations.literal: From Wei age onward, those promoted and summoned by appointment, and serving clerks, facing audience receiving order, although self declining unable, to the end none were willing to yield to those who surpassed self.
translations.idiomatic: Since the Wei dynasty, appointees and serving officials alike, even when they protest that they are unfit, never yield to someone more capable.

sentences.zh: 夫推讓之風息，爭競之心生。

translations.literal: When pushing-yielding’s wind ceases, striving-competing’s heart is born.
translations.idiomatic: When yielding dies, the scramble for place begins.

sentences.zh: 孔子曰，上興讓則下不爭，明讓不興下必爭也。

translations.literal: Confucius said, superiors raise yielding then inferiors do not contend; clarifying yielding not rising inferiors must contend.
translations.idiomatic: Confucius said that when superiors encourage yielding, inferiors do not fight; when yielding is not honored below, strife is inevitable.

sentences.zh: 推讓之道興，則賢能之人日見推舉；

translations.literal: Pushing-yielding’s way rises, then worthy able men daily see pushing and raising;
translations.idiomatic: Where yielding flourishes, able men are advanced every day;

sentences.zh: 爭競之心生，則賢能之人日見謗毀。

translations.literal: striving-competing’s heart born, then worthy able men daily see slander and ruin.
translations.idiomatic: where rivalry rules, they are slandered every day.

sentences.zh: 夫爭者之欲自先，甚惡能者之先，不能無毀也。

translations.literal: As for contenders’ desire to be self first, greatly hating able ones’ first, cannot be without ruin.
translations.idiomatic: Schemers want to be first themselves and loathe anyone ahead of them; slander follows inevitably.

sentences.zh: 故孔墨不能免世之謗己，況不及孔墨者乎！

translations.literal: Therefore Confucius and Mo Di could not escape the age’s slandering self, how much less those not reaching Confucius and Mo Di!
translations.idiomatic: Even Confucius and Mozi could not escape calumny; what hope have lesser men?”

sentences.zh: 議者僉然言，世少高名之才，朝廷不有大才之人可以為大官者。

translations.literal: Discussers all alike say, the age lacks high-name talent; the court does not have great-talent men who can be great officials.
translations.idiomatic: Critics all insist the age lacks men of towering reputation and that the court has no one fit for the highest posts.

sentences.zh: 山澤人小官吏亦復雲，朝廷之士雖有大官名德，皆不及往時人也。

translations.literal: Mountain-marsh men petty clerks also again say, court gentlemen although have great office name virtue, all do not reach past-time men.
translations.idiomatic: Rustic clerks echo the charge that today’s grandees, however titled, cannot match men of former days.

sentences.zh: 餘以為此二言皆失之矣。

translations.literal: I consider these two sayings all miss it.
translations.idiomatic: Both verdicts are wrong.

sentences.zh: 非時獨乏賢也，時不貴讓。

translations.literal: It is not that the age alone lacks worthies; the age does not esteem yielding.
translations.idiomatic: The problem is not a shortage of worthies but a culture that scorns yielding.

sentences.zh: 一人有先眾之譽，毀必隨之，名不得成使之然也。

translations.literal: One person has ahead-of-crowd’s praise, ruin surely follows it; name cannot be completed makes it thus.
translations.idiomatic: Whoever outshines the pack is torn down; reputations cannot mature because of it.

sentences.zh: 雖令稷契復存，亦不復能全其名矣。

translations.literal: Even if making Ji and Xie again exist, also again cannot preserve their names.
translations.idiomatic: Even Ji and Xie reborn could not keep their names intact in such a climate.

sentences.zh: 能否混雜，優劣不分，士無素定之價，官職有缺，主選之吏不知所用，但案官次而舉之。

translations.literal: Able and unable mix confused; excellence and inferiority not divided; gentlemen lack plain-fixed price; offices have gaps; masters of selection clerks do not know what to use; only investigate office order and raise them.
translations.idiomatic: Able and inept are jumbled together, merit goes unrecognized, and gentlemen have no settled standing; when posts open, appointing officials have no guide but seniority.

sentences.zh: 同才之人先用者，非勢家之子，則必為有勢者之所念也。

translations.literal: Among same-talent men those first used, if not powerful-house sons, then must be those powerful ones ponder.
translations.idiomatic: Among equals, the first promoted are either sons of great houses or men favored by the powerful.

sentences.zh: 非能獨賢，因其先用之資，而復遷之無已。

translations.literal: Not able alone worthy; because of their first-used capital, again promote them without end.
translations.idiomatic: They are not uniquely virtuous; their head start feeds endless promotion.

sentences.zh: 遷之無已，不勝其任之病發矣。

translations.literal: Promoting them without end, not bearing their duty’s illness breaks out.
translations.idiomatic: Endless advancement soon exposes men who cannot bear their responsibilities.

sentences.zh: 觀在官之人，政績無聞，自非勢家之子，率多因資次而進也。

translations.literal: Observe those holding office: administrative achievement unheard; if not self powerful-house sons, mostly many because of seniority order advance.
translations.idiomatic: Look at men in office: few have real achievements; unless they are wellborn, most have climbed by seniority alone.

sentences.zh: 向令天下貴讓，士必由於見讓而後名成，名成而官乃得用之。

translations.literal: Suppose we ordered the realm to esteem yielding; gentlemen must by being yielded to then name is completed, name completed and office then can use them.
translations.idiomatic: If yielding were honored across the realm, a man would first have to be publicly deferred to before his name was made; only then would office rightly take him up.

sentences.zh: 諸名行不立之人，在官無政績之稱，讓之者必矣，官無因得而用之也。

translations.literal: Those whose name and conduct are not established, in office without administrative achievement’s praise, those who yield to them will be certain; office has no cause thereby to use them.
translations.idiomatic: Men of no established reputation who achieve nothing in office would surely be passed over in favor of others, and the state would have no excuse to employ them.

sentences.zh: 所以見用不息者，由讓道廢，因資用人之有失久矣。

translations.literal: The reason those seen employed without cease is because yielding way is abandoned; relying on seniority to employ men’s having error is long.
translations.idiomatic: Mediocre men stay in office because yielding has died out and appointment by seniority alone has misgoverned us for ages.

sentences.zh: 故自漢魏以來，時開大舉，令眾官各舉所知，唯才所任，不限階次，如此者甚數矣。

translations.literal: Therefore from Han and Wei onward, times opened great raising, ordering host of officials each raise those they know, only talent what is appointed, not limited rank order; like this has been very numerous.
translations.idiomatic: Since Han and Wei, the court has often ordered a general call for recommendations—each official to name men he knew, talent the only criterion, rank no barrier—and such measures have been tried again and again.

sentences.zh: 其所舉必有當者，不聞時有擢用，不知何誰最賢故也。

translations.literal: Among those raised there must be fitting ones; not heard that time had promotions and employments; not knowing who is most worthy is the reason.
translations.idiomatic: Some nominees must have been fit, yet we never hear who was actually promoted, because no one can tell who was worthiest.

sentences.zh: 所舉必有不當，而罪不加，不知何誰最不肖也。

translations.literal: Among those raised there must be unfitting ones, yet punishment not applied; not knowing who is most unworthy.
translations.idiomatic: Some nominees must have been unfit, yet no one is punished—again because no one can pick out the worst.

sentences.zh: 所以不可得知，由當時之人莫肯相推，賢愚之名不別，令其如此。

translations.literal: The reason it cannot be known is because people of the time none willing mutually to defer; worthy and foolish’s names not distinguished; orders it like this.
translations.idiomatic: The confusion comes from everyone refusing to yield place, so worthy and worthless look the same.

sentences.zh: 舉者知在上者察不能審，故敢漫舉而進之。

translations.literal: Those who raise know those above examine unable to be careful; therefore dare carelessly raise and advance them.
translations.idiomatic: Recommenders know superiors cannot vet every name, so they nominate recklessly.

sentences.zh: 或舉所賢，因及所念，一頓而至，人數猥多，各言所舉者賢，加之高狀，相似如一，難得而分矣。

translations.literal: Some raise those they esteem, thereby reaching those they favor; one batch arrives; people’s number excessively many; each says those they raised are worthy, add to them high descriptions, similar as one; hard to obtain and divide.
translations.idiomatic: Some push their favorites in a single mass nomination; the lists swell, every sponsor swears his picks are paragons and pads their files with identical praise, so the truth cannot be sorted out.

sentences.zh: 參錯相亂，真偽同貫，更復由此而甚。

translations.literal: Mixed wrong confused; true and false same thread; again further by this becomes extreme.
translations.idiomatic: Truth and falsehood are tangled together, and the mess only deepens.

sentences.zh: 雖舉者不能盡忠之罪，亦由上開聽察之路濫，令其爾也。

translations.literal: Although raisers cannot exhaust loyalty’s fault, also because superiors open hearing-examination’s road excessive, orders it thus.
translations.idiomatic: Recommenders share the blame, but the throne invited the abuse by opening indiscriminate channels of review.

sentences.zh: 昔齊王好聽竽聲，必令三百人合吹而後聽之，廩以數人之俸。

translations.literal: Formerly the king of Qi loved listening to yu sound, always ordered three hundred men together blow then listened, granary-paid with several men’s salaries.
translations.idiomatic: The king of Qi loved massed mouth-organs and would hear no fewer than three hundred players at once, paying each band the stipend of several ordinary musicians.

sentences.zh: 南郭先生不知吹竽者也，以三百人合吹可以容其不知，因請為王吹竽，虛食數人之俸。

translations.literal: Mr. Southwall did not know blowing yu; because three hundred together blowing could accommodate his not knowing, thereupon asked to blow yu for the king, empty-ate several men’s salaries.
translations.idiomatic: Mr. Southwall could not play at all, but hid inside the three-hundred-man ensemble, volunteered for the royal band, and drew several musicians’ pay for nothing.

sentences.zh: 嗣王覺而改之，難彰先王之過。

translations.literal: The succeeding king perceived and changed it, hard to display the former king’s fault.
translations.idiomatic: The new king saw the fraud but hesitated to shame his father’s memory.

sentences.zh: 乃下令曰：「吾之好聞竽聲有甚于先王，欲一一列而聽之。

translations.literal: Thereupon issued order saying, “My liking to hear yu sound is greater than the former king; I wish one by one array and listen to them.”
translations.idiomatic: He therefore proclaimed: “I love the mouth-organ even more than my father did—I mean to hear each player perform solo.”

sentences.zh: 」先生于此逃矣。

translations.literal: ” The gentleman at this fled.
translations.idiomatic: At that Mr. Southwall fled.

sentences.zh: 推賢之風不立，濫舉之法不改，則南郭先生之徒盈於朝矣。

translations.literal: If pushing worthies’ wind is not established, wanton raising’s law not changed, then Mr. Southwall’s kind fill the court.
translations.idiomatic: Until we revive real recommendation and fix promiscuous nomination, the court will swarm with Southwalls.

sentences.zh: 才高守道之士日退，馳走有勢之門日多矣。

translations.literal: High-talent way-keeping gentlemen daily withdraw; galloping-running to powerful gates daily many.
translations.idiomatic: Able men of principle withdraw while sycophants rush the doors of the mighty in ever greater numbers.

sentences.zh: 雖國有典刑，弗能禁矣。

translations.literal: Although the state has statutes and punishments, cannot forbid.
translations.idiomatic: Statute law alone cannot stop it.

sentences.zh: 夫讓道不興之弊，非徒賢人在下位，不得時進也，國之良臣荷重任者，亦將以漸受罪退矣。

translations.literal: The harm of yielding way not rising is not only worthies in lower positions unable timely to advance; the state’s good ministers bearing heavy burden also will by degrees suffer punishment and withdraw.
translations.idiomatic: The evil of suppressing yielding is not merely that talent languishes below; even good ministers in heavy posts will in time be hounded from office.

sentences.zh: 何以知其然也？

translations.literal: By what know it is thus?
translations.idiomatic: How do we know?

sentences.zh: 孔子以為顏氏之子不貳過耳，明非聖人皆有過。

translations.literal: Confucius thought the Yan clan’s son did not twice err only; clarifies that not sages all have faults.
translations.idiomatic: Confucius said only Yan Hui never repeated a mistake—meaning every man short of sagehood errs.

sentences.zh: 寵貴之地欲之者多矣，惡賢能者塞其路，其過而毀之者亦多矣。

translations.literal: Doted-noble positions—those who desire them are many; those who hate worthies block their road; those who by fault ruin them also are many.
translations.idiomatic: Coveted posts attract many suitors; the envious bar the able and seize on the slightest slip to destroy them.

sentences.zh: 夫謗毀之生，非徒空設，必因人之微過而甚之者也。

translations.literal: Slander and ruin’s birth is not merely empty setup; must be because of men’s slight faults and magnifies them.
translations.idiomatic: Slander is never baseless—it magnifies a man’s smallest lapses.

sentences.zh: 譭謗之言數聞，在上者雖欲弗納，不能不杖所聞，因事之來而微察之也，無以，其驗至矣。

translations.literal: Defamation’s words repeatedly heard; those above although wish not to accept, cannot but staff what is heard; because matters come and slightly examine them; nothing to do—its verification arrives.
translations.idiomatic: Rumors pile up until even a reluctant ruler feels bound to heed them, probes each incident, and finds seeming proof.

sentences.zh: 得其驗，安得不理其罪。

translations.literal: Obtaining its verification, how can one not regulate their crime?
translations.idiomatic: Once “proof” appears, punishment must follow.

sentences.zh: 若知而縱之，王之威日衰，令之不行自此始矣。

translations.literal: If knowing yet indulging them, the king’s awe daily wanes; orders’ not being enacted from this begins.
translations.idiomatic: To ignore verified guilt would drain royal authority and mark the start of disobedience.

sentences.zh: 知而皆理之，受罪退者稍多，大臣有不自固之心。

translations.literal: Knowing and all regulating them, those suffering punishment and withdrawal gradually many; great ministers have not self-firm hearts.
translations.idiomatic: Punish every case and dismissed ministers multiply, until senior officials no longer feel secure.

sentences.zh: 夫賢才不進，貴臣日疏，此有國者之深憂也。

translations.literal: Worthy talent not advancing, noble ministers daily estranged—this is those who hold the state’s deep worry.
translations.idiomatic: Barred talent and alienated ministers are a ruler’s gravest concern.

sentences.zh: 《詩》曰：「受祿不讓，至於已斯亡。

translations.literal: The Odes says, “Receiving salary not yielding, reaching to self this perishes.”
translations.idiomatic: The Book of Odes says, ‘They took emoluments without yielding—thus they brought ruin on themselves.’

sentences.zh: 」不讓之人憂亡不暇，而望其益國朝，不亦難乎！

translations.literal: ” Those who do not yield—worry about ruin without leisure—yet hope they benefit state and court: is it not hard!
translations.idiomatic: Men who never yield busy themselves dodging disaster—can we expect them to enrich the realm?”

sentences.zh: 竊以為改此俗甚易耳。

translations.literal: I privately think changing this custom is very easy.
translations.idiomatic: I believe this habit could be changed with ease.

sentences.zh: 何以知之？

translations.literal: By what know it?
translations.idiomatic: Why?

sentences.zh: 夫一時在官之人，雖雜有凡猥之才，其中賢明者亦多矣，豈可謂皆不知讓賢為貴邪！

translations.literal: As for men in office at one time, although mixed with vulgar base talent, among them worthy and bright ones also are many; how can it be said all do not know yielding worthies as precious!
translations.idiomatic: Officialdom always mixes mediocrities with many who do know that yielding to the better man is right.

sentences.zh: 直以其時皆不讓，習以成俗，故遂不為耳。

translations.literal: Simply because at that time all did not yield, habit thereby became custom; therefore in the end did not do it.
translations.idiomatic: They simply follow a custom of never yielding—it is habit, not ignorance.

sentences.zh: 人臣初除，皆通表上聞，名之謝章，所由來尚矣。

translations.literal: Ministers at first appointment all communicate memorial upward heard; name it thanks memorial; the origin is long.
translations.idiomatic: New appointees have always memorialized their thanks to the throne—the practice is ancient.

sentences.zh: 原謝章之本意，欲進賢能以謝國恩也。

translations.literal: Trace thanks memorial’s original intent: desired to advance worthy ability thereby to thank state grace.
translations.idiomatic: The memorial of thanks was meant to recommend better men in return for imperial favor.

sentences.zh: 昔舜以禹為司空，禹拜稽首，讓於稷契及咎繇。

translations.literal: Formerly Shun took Yu as Minister of Works; Yu bowed head to ground, yielded to Ji, Xie, and Gao Yao.
translations.idiomatic: When Shun made Yu Minister of Works, Yu kowtowed and ceded the honor to Ji, Xie, and Gao Yao.

sentences.zh: 使益為虞官，讓於硃虎、熊、羆。

translations.literal: Ordered Yi as Yu official, yielded to Zhu Hu, Xiong, and Pi.
translations.idiomatic: When Yi was made forest warden, he yielded to Zhu Hu, Xiong, and Pi.

sentences.zh: 使伯夷典三禮，讓于夔龍。

translations.literal: Ordered Boyi to manage three rites, yielded to Kui and Long.
translations.idiomatic: Boyi was put in charge of the three classes of rites but named Kui and Long instead.

sentences.zh: 唐虞之時，眾官初除，莫不皆讓也。

translations.literal: In Tang and Yu’s time, host of officials at first appointment, none not all yielded.
translations.idiomatic: Under Yao and Shun every new minister deferred to rivals.

sentences.zh: 謝章之義，蓋取於此。

translations.literal: Thanks memorial’s meaning, covers taken from this.
translations.idiomatic: The thanks memorial harks back to that ideal.

sentences.zh: 《書》記之者，欲以永世作則。

translations.literal: The Document records it, desiring thereby for ages to make model.
translations.idiomatic: The Book of Documents preserves the stories to be an eternal model.

sentences.zh: 季世所用，不賢不能讓賢，虛謝見用之恩而已。

translations.literal: Decadent age’s use: not worthy unable to yield worthies; empty thanks for seen-employment’s grace only.
translations.idiomatic: Later ages hollowed the rite into empty gratitude from men neither able nor willing to yield.

sentences.zh: 相承不變，習俗之失也。

translations.literal: Mutually inheriting unchanged—custom’s failure.
translations.idiomatic: Unthinking continuity turned it into a vulgar habit.

sentences.zh: 夫敘用之官得通章表者，其讓賢推能乃通，其不能有所讓徒費簡紙者，皆絕不通。

translations.literal: As for order-employing officials who can communicate memorials: their yielding worthies pushing ability then passes; those unable to have anything to yield, vainly wasting slip paper—all cut off not passing.
translations.idiomatic: Let every appointing officer accept only memorials that name worthier men; bar empty thanks that waste paper.

sentences.zh: 人臣初除，各思推賢能而讓之矣，讓之文付主者掌之。

translations.literal: Ministers at first appointment, each thinks push worthy ability and yield to them; yielding’s text entrust to masters to keep.
translations.idiomatic: Each new minister would propose a worthier candidate; those nominations go on file with the registrar.

sentences.zh: 三司有缺，擇三司所讓最多者而用之。

translations.literal: When the Three Dukes have a vacancy, select among those the Three Dukes yielded to most and use him.
translations.idiomatic: Fill a vacancy among the Three Dukes with the man most often yielded to by sitting dukes.

sentences.zh: 此為一公缺，三公已豫選之矣。

translations.literal: This is one duke vacant; three dukes already beforehand selected him.
translations.idiomatic: Thus one post is filled from a pool the three dukes have already ranked.

sentences.zh: 且主選之吏，不必任公而選三公，不如令三公自共選一公為詳也。

translations.literal: Moreover masters of selection clerks need not appoint dukes to select Three Dukes; better order Three Dukes themselves together select one duke—this is more careful.
translations.idiomatic: Better the Three Dukes choose one of their own than leave it to a personnel clerk who need not be a duke himself.

sentences.zh: 四征缺，擇四征所讓最多而用之，此為一征缺，四征已豫選之矣，必詳於停缺而令主者選四征也。

translations.literal: Four Expeditions vacant: select among Four Expeditions those yielded to most and use; this is one expedition vacant; Four Expeditions already beforehand selected; must be more careful than halted vacancy and order masters select Four Expeditions.
translations.idiomatic: Do the same for the four expeditionary commands: when one opens, pick the candidate most deferred to by all four—a far sounder method than freezing the post and letting a clerk pick.

sentences.zh: 尚書缺，擇尚書所讓最多者而用之，此為八尚書共選一尚書，詳于臨缺令主者選八尚書也。

translations.literal: Masters of Writing vacant: select among Masters of Writing those yielded to most and use; this is eight Masters of Writing together select one Master of Writing—more careful than facing vacancy ordering masters select eight Masters of Writing.
translations.idiomatic: For a vacancy among the Masters of Writing, let the eight incumbents jointly nominate the man most yielded to—wiser than a hurried personnel shuffle.

sentences.zh: 郡守缺，擇眾郡所讓最多者而用之，詳于任主者令選百郡守也。

translations.literal: Commandery governor vacant: select among host of commanderies those yielded to most and use—more careful than appointing masters ordering selection of hundred commandery governors.
translations.idiomatic: Governorships should go to the men most widely recommended by other governors, not to whoever a central clerk favors.

sentences.zh: 夫以眾官百郡之讓，與主者共相比，不可同歲而論也。

translations.literal: As for using host of officials hundred commanderies’ yielding compared with masters together—cannot in same year discuss.
translations.idiomatic: Peer nomination across hundreds of posts bears no comparison to a clerk ticking names in one sitting.

sentences.zh: 雖復令三府參舉官，本不委以舉選之任，各不能以根其心也。

translations.literal: Although again ordering Three Offices participate raising officials, fundamentally not entrust them raising-selection’s duty; each cannot thereby root their hearts.
translations.idiomatic: Even when the Three Offices “assist” in selection, they are not truly charged with it and never invest their hearts in the outcome.

sentences.zh: 其所用心者裁之不二三，但令主者案官次而舉之，不用精也。

translations.literal: What they use heart on—trim it not two or three; only order masters investigate office order and raise them; not using refinement.
translations.idiomatic: They skim two or three names and tell the clerk to go by seniority—no care at all.

sentences.zh: 賢愚皆讓，百姓耳目盡為國耳目。

translations.literal: Worthy and foolish all yield; hundred surnames’ ears and eyes all become the state’s ears and eyes.
translations.idiomatic: If every man must yield, the people become the state’s eyes and ears.

sentences.zh: 夫人情爭則欲毀己所不知，讓則競推於勝己。

translations.literal: As for human feeling: striving then desires ruin what self does not know; yielding then competes to push those who surpass self.
translations.idiomatic: Rivalry breeds slander of the unknown; yielding makes men lift up their betters.

sentences.zh: 故世爭則毀譽交錯，優劣不分，難得而讓也。

translations.literal: Therefore age striving then praise and blame interweave; excellence and inferiority not divided; hard to obtain yielding.
translations.idiomatic: In a contentious age praise and blame tangle until merit is invisible and yielding impossible.

sentences.zh: 時讓則賢智顯出，能否之美歷歷相次，不可得而亂也。

translations.literal: Age yielding then worthy wisdom appears out; able and unable’s beauty clear and successive—cannot obtain and confuse.
translations.idiomatic: When yielding is the fashion, talent stands out in clear order and cannot be confounded.

sentences.zh: 當此時也，能退身修已者，讓之者多矣。

translations.literal: At this time, those able to withdraw body and cultivate self—those who yield to them are many.
translations.idiomatic: Then men who retire to perfect themselves win many sponsors.

sentences.zh: 雖欲守貧賤，不可得也。

translations.literal: Although wishing to keep poverty and low status, cannot obtain it.
translations.idiomatic: They cannot stay obscure even if they wish to.

sentences.zh: 馳騖進趣而欲人見讓，猶卻行而求前也。

translations.literal: Galloping-rushing advancement ambition yet desiring people see yielding—is like walking backward seeking forward.
translations.idiomatic: To scramble for place yet expect others to yield is to walk backward and hope to advance.

sentences.zh: 夫如此，愚智咸知進身求通，非修之於己則無由矣。

translations.literal: Like this, foolish and wise all know advancing self seeking penetration—if not cultivating in self then there is no means.
translations.idiomatic: Then fool and sage alike see that advancement lies in self-cultivation or nowhere.

sentences.zh: 游外求者，於此相隨而歸矣。

translations.literal: Those wandering outside seeking—at this follow one another and return.
translations.idiomatic: Adventurers who sought shortcuts would give them up and come home.
