sentences.zh: 浮聲虛論，不禁而自息矣。

translations.literal: Floating sounds empty discussions—not forbidden and self cease.
translations.idiomatic: Empty gossip would die without being banned.

sentences.zh: 人人無所用其心，任眾人之議，而天下自化矣。

translations.literal: Every person nothing to use their heart on; entrust crowd’s discussions—and the realm self transforms.
translations.idiomatic: Rulers need not scheme; trust public consensus and the realm orders itself.

sentences.zh: 不言之化行，巍巍之美於此著矣。

translations.literal: Non-speaking transformation practiced; towering beauty at this is manifest.
translations.idiomatic: Silent transformation unfolds, and the majesty of true rule appears.

sentences.zh: 讓可以致此，豈可不務之哉！

translations.literal: Yielding can bring this about—how can one not pursue it!
translations.idiomatic: Yielding can achieve this—how can we neglect it?”

sentences.zh: 《春秋傳》曰：「范宣子之讓，其下皆讓。

translations.literal: The Spring and Autumn Tradition says, “Fan Xuanzi’s yielding—those below him all yielded.”
translations.idiomatic: The Zuo Commentary says, ‘When Fan Xuanzi yielded, his subordinates yielded in turn.’

sentences.zh: 欒黶雖汰，弗敢違也。

translations.literal: Luan Yan although arrogant, dared not disobey.
translations.idiomatic: Even the reckless Luan Yan dared not defy the example.

sentences.zh: 晉國以平，數世賴之。

translations.literal: Jin state thereby was pacified; several generations relied on it.
translations.idiomatic: Jin knew peace for generations because of it.

sentences.zh: 」上世之化也，君子尚能而讓其下，小人力農以事其上，上下有禮，讒慝遠黜，由不爭也。

translations.literal: ” Upper age’s transformation: gentlemen esteem ability and yield to those below; petty men labor farming to serve those above; above and below have ritual; slander and evil far dismissed—because of not contending.
translations.idiomatic: Such was the teaching of high antiquity: gentlemen honored ability and stepped aside for subordinates, commoners farmed to support their betters, rank observed ritual, and slander vanished because nothing was contested.”

sentences.zh: 及其亂也，國家之弊，恆必由之。

translations.literal: When it comes to their disorder, the state’s ills always must come from this.
translations.idiomatic: When that order collapses, national ruin always follows.

sentences.zh: 篤論了了如此。

translations.literal: Earnest discussion clear thus.
translations.idiomatic: The moral is plain.

sentences.zh: 在朝君子典選大官，能不以人廢言，舉而行之，各以讓賢舉能為先務，則群才猥出，能否殊別，蓋世之功，莫大於此。

translations.literal: Gentlemen at court who manage selection great offices—if able not because of person discard words, raise and practice them, each taking yielding worthies raising ability as first task—then host of talents abundantly emerge; able and unable markedly distinguished; age-covering achievement, nothing greater than this.
translations.idiomatic: If ministers in charge of appointments heed this advice despite its author and put yielding first, talent will pour forth, competence will sort itself, and no reform would do more good.

sentences.zh: 泰始初，進爵為伯，累遷少府。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Taishi, advanced noble rank to earl, promoted in stages to Privy Treasurer.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Taishi his fief was raised to earl’s rank and he rose to Privy Treasurer.

sentences.zh: 咸甯中為太常。

translations.literal: In Xianning he was Minister of Ceremonies.
translations.idiomatic: During Xianning he served as Minister of Ceremonies.

sentences.zh: 轉尚書。

translations.literal: Transferred to Master of Writing.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to the Masters of Writing.

sentences.zh: 杜預之伐吳也，寔以本官行鎮南軍司。

translations.literal: When Du Yu campaigned against Wu, Shi by original office acted South Garrisoning Army director.
translations.idiomatic: During Du Yu’s conquest of Wu, Liu Shi served as army director on the southern command staff in his regular capacity.

sentences.zh: 初，寔妻盧氏生子躋而卒，華氏將以女妻之。

translations.literal: At first, Shi’s wife Lady Lu bore son Ji then died; the Hua clan was about to take a daughter and marry him.
translations.idiomatic: Shi’s first wife, Lady Lu, bore a son, Ji, and died; the Hua family then proposed a daughter as his next wife.

sentences.zh: 寔弟智諫曰：「華家類貪，必破門戶。

translations.literal: Shi’s younger brother Zhi remonstrated, “The Hua clan is by kind greedy; surely will ruin the gate and household.”
translations.idiomatic: His brother Zhi warned him, “The Huas are a grasping clan—they will ruin our house.”

sentences.zh: 」辭之不得，竟婚華氏而生子夏。

translations.literal: ” Declining it could not succeed; in the end married Hua clan and bore son Xia.
translations.idiomatic: He could not refuse; he married into the Huas and fathered a son, Xia.

sentences.zh: 寔竟坐夏受賂，免官。

translations.literal: Shi in the end sat because Xia accepted bribes, dismissed from office.
translations.idiomatic: Shi was stripped of office when Xia was convicted of taking bribes.

sentences.zh: 頃之為大司農，又以夏罪免。

translations.literal: Presently he was Minister of Agriculture, again because of Xia’s crime dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: Soon named Minister of Agriculture, he lost that post too over Xia’s guilt.

sentences.zh: 寔每還州裏，鄉人載酒肉以候之。

translations.literal: Whenever Shi returned to the commandery, townsfolk loaded wine and meat to await him.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever Shi visited his home commandery, villagers brought wine and meat to greet him.

sentences.zh: 寔難逆其意，輒共啖而返其餘。

translations.literal: Shi hard to oppose their intent, always together ate and returned the remainder.
translations.idiomatic: Unwilling to spurn their kindness, he shared the meal and sent the leftovers back.

sentences.zh: 或謂寔曰：「君行高一世，而諸子不能遵。

translations.literal: Someone said to Shi, “Your lordship’s conduct is high for one age, yet the various sons cannot follow.”
translations.idiomatic: Someone said to him, “Your conduct towers above the age, yet your sons do not follow it.”

sentences.zh: 何不旦夕切磋，使知過而自改邪！

translations.literal: Why not morning and evening polish together, make them know fault and self-reform!”
translations.idiomatic: Why not coach them daily until they mend their ways?”

sentences.zh: 」寔曰：「吾之所行，是所聞見，不相祖習，豈復教誨之所得乎！

translations.literal: ” Shi said, “What I practice is what I heard and saw; not mutually inheriting habit—how again is what instruction obtains!”
translations.idiomatic: Shi replied, “My conduct comes from what I saw and heard; it is not something sons pick up by family habit—how can lectures instill it?”

sentences.zh: 」世以寔言為當。

translations.literal: ” The age deemed Shi’s words correct.
translations.idiomatic: Contemporaries judged him right.

sentences.zh: 後起為國子祭酒、散騎常侍。

translations.literal: Later he rose as Libationer of the National University, Cavalier Attendant-in-Ordinary.
translations.idiomatic: He was later recalled as Libationer of the Imperial Academy and Cavalier Attendant-in-Ordinary.

sentences.zh: 湣懷太子初封廣陵王，高選師友，以寔為師。

translations.literal: When Crown Prince Minhuai was first enfeoffed Prince of Guangling, highly selected teachers and friends, took Shi as teacher.
translations.idiomatic: When the heir Minhuai was first made Prince of Guangling, the court chose eminent tutors and named Shi his principal teacher.

sentences.zh: 元康初，進爵為侯，累遷太子太保，加侍中、特進、右光祿大夫、開府儀同三司，領冀州都督。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Yuankang, advanced noble rank to marquis, promoted in stages to Junior Mentor to the crown prince, added Palace Attendant, Specially Advanced, Right Grand Master of Splendid Happiness, office opening ceremonial equal Three Dukes, heading Ji Province military governor.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Yuankang he was promoted to marquis, rose to Junior Mentor to the heir, and accumulated the titles Palace Attendant, Specially Advanced, Right Grand Master of Splendid Happiness, and commander with ceremonial parity to the Three Dukes while directing military affairs in Ji Province.

sentences.zh: 九年，策拜司空，遷太保，轉太傅。

translations.literal: In the ninth year, by document appointed Minister of Works, promoted Grand Guardian, transferred Grand Tutor.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year he was appointed Minister of Works by patent, then Grand Guardian, then Grand Tutor.

sentences.zh: 太安初，寔以老病遜位，賜安車駟馬、錢百萬，以侯就第。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Tai’an, Shi because of old age and illness yielded position, gifted secure carriage four-horse team, cash one million, as marquis went to mansion.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Tai’an he resigned on grounds of age and ill health, receiving a comfortable carriage, a four-horse team, and a million cash to retire home as a marquis.

sentences.zh: 及長沙成都之相攻也，寔為軍人所掠，潛歸鄉里。

translations.literal: When Changsha and Chengdu mutually attacked, Shi was plundered by soldiers, secretly returned to hometown.
translations.idiomatic: During the war between the princes of Changsha and Chengdu, soldiers plundered him and he slipped away to his native place.

sentences.zh: 三年，詔曰：「昔虞任五臣，致垂拱之化，漢相蕭何，興寧一之譽，故能光隆於當時，垂裕於百代。

translations.literal: In the third year, an edict said, “Formerly Yu employed five ministers, achieved hands-folded transformation; Han minister Xiao He, raised unified calm’s praise; therefore able to shine grand at the time, hang abundance for hundred generations.”
translations.idiomatic: In the third year an edict declared: “Yu employed five ministers and ruled with folded hands; Chancellor Xiao He of Han won fame for unifying the realm—thus they glorified their own age and left an example for all time.”

sentences.zh: 朕紹天明命，臨御萬邦，所以崇顯政道者，亦賴之於元臣庶尹，畢力股肱，以副至望。

translations.literal: We continue Heaven’s bright mandate, face and govern myriad regions; the means by which we exalt and display governing the Way also rely on chief ministers and many directors, exhaust strength as thigh and arm, to match utmost hope.”
translations.idiomatic: We have inherited Heaven’s charge and rule the myriad lands; to exalt good government We depend on chief ministers and high officials to give their utmost as Our arms and legs and meet Our deepest expectations.”

sentences.zh: 而君年耆告老，確然難違。

translations.literal: Yet your lordship by years old announced old, firmly hard to oppose.”
translations.idiomatic: Yet you, venerable in years, have begged to retire, and your resolve cannot be denied.”

sentences.zh: 今聽君以侯就第，位居三司之上，秩祿准舊，賜几杖不朝及宅一區。

translations.literal: Now We listen to your lordship as marquis go to mansion; position ranks above Three Dukes; salary and grain follow old; gift stool and staff, not attend court, and one residence.”
translations.idiomatic: We grant you leave to retire home as a marquis with rank above the Three Dukes, stipends as before, a stool and staff excusing you from court, and a residence.”

sentences.zh: 國之大政，將就諮於君，副朕意焉。

translations.literal: The state’s great policies will near consult with your lordship, matching Our intent.”
translations.idiomatic: On weighty affairs of state We shall still seek your counsel—such is Our wish.”

sentences.zh: 」歲余薨，時年九十一，諡曰元。

translations.literal: ” After a little over a year he died; at the time age ninety-one; posthumous name Yuan.
translations.idiomatic: A little over a year later he died at ninety-one and received the posthumous title “Yuan” (“Primordial”).

sentences.zh: 寔少貧窶，杖策徒行，每所憩止，不累主人，薪水之事，皆自營給。

translations.literal: Shi in youth was poor; leaning staff walked on foot; wherever he rested, did not burden host; firewood and water matters, all self supplied.
translations.idiomatic: In youth he was destitute, walked with staff in hand, and wherever he lodged imposed nothing on his host—he fetched his own fuel and water.

sentences.zh: 及位望通顯，每崇儉素，不尚華麗。

translations.literal: When position and fame were eminent, he always esteemed frugality and plainness, did not esteem splendor and beauty.
translations.idiomatic: Even after he rose to prominence he clung to plain austerity and shunned display.

sentences.zh: 嘗詣石崇家，如廁，見有絳紋帳，裀褥甚麗，兩婢持香囊。

translations.literal: He once went to Shi Chong’s house, went to toilet, saw there was crimson-patterned curtain, cushions and bedding very lovely, two maids holding incense sachets.
translations.idiomatic: On a visit to Shi Chong he stepped into what he thought was a lavatory and found crimson brocade hangings, sumptuous bedding, and two maids bearing sachets of perfume.

sentences.zh: 寔便退，笑謂崇曰：「誤入卿內。

translations.literal: Shi then withdrew, laughed and said to Chong, “Mistakenly entered your inner chambers.”
translations.idiomatic: Shi backed out and said with a smile, “I blundered into your private rooms.”

sentences.zh: 」崇曰：「是廁耳。

translations.literal: ” Chong said, “This is the toilet.”
translations.idiomatic: Chong said, “That was the privy.”

sentences.zh: 」寔曰：「貧士未嘗得此。

translations.literal: ” Shi said, “A poor scholar has never obtained this.”
translations.idiomatic: Shi replied, “A poor scholar like me has never seen a privy like that.”

sentences.zh: 」乃更如他廁。

translations.literal: ” Thereupon changed to another toilet.
translations.idiomatic: He used another lavatory instead.

sentences.zh: 雖處榮寵，居無第宅，所得俸祿，贍恤親故。

translations.literal: Although dwelling in glory and favor, he had no mansion; obtained salary and grain, supported and relieved kin and old friends.
translations.idiomatic: Though honored at court, he owned no grand house and spent his salary supporting kinsmen and old friends.

sentences.zh: 雖禮教陵遲，而行己以正。

translations.literal: Although ritual teaching declined, in conducting himself he used rectitude.
translations.idiomatic: Even as public morals slipped, he held himself to the straight path.

sentences.zh: 喪妻為廬杖之制，終喪不禦內。

translations.literal: Mourning wife he made hut and staff regulations; to end of mourning did not take inner chambers.
translations.idiomatic: When his wife died he observed the full mourning hut and staff rites and took no concubine until they ended.

sentences.zh: 輕薄者笑之，寔不以介意。

translations.literal: Frivolous ones laughed at him; Shi did not take it to heart.
translations.idiomatic: Wits mocked him; he paid them no mind.

sentences.zh: 自少及老，篤學不倦，雖居職務，卷弗離手。

translations.literal: From youth to old age, devoted to learning without weariness; although holding office duties, scroll did not leave hand.
translations.idiomatic: From youth to age he studied tirelessly and never set a book aside, even in office.

sentences.zh: 尤精《三傳》，辨正《公羊》，以為衛輒不應辭以王父命，祭仲失為臣之節，舉此二端以明臣子之體，遂行於世。

translations.literal: He especially mastered the Three Traditions, debated and corrected the Gongyang commentary, thought Wei Zhe ought not decline citing grandfather’s order, Ji Zhong lost minister’s integrity; raising these two ends to clarify minister-son’s substance, thereupon practiced in the world.
translations.idiomatic: He excelled in the Three Commentaries and revised readings of the Gongyang, arguing that Prince Zhe of Wei was wrong to refuse the throne citing his grandfather’s command and that Ji Zhong had betrayed a minister’s duty; these two cases became his model of how subjects and sons should behave, and his reading won wide acceptance.

sentences.zh: 又撰《春秋條例》二十卷。

translations.literal: Also composed Spring and Autumn Regulations twenty scrolls.
translations.idiomatic: He also compiled twenty fascicles of Spring and Autumn precedents.

sentences.zh: 有二子，躋、夏。

translations.literal: He had two sons, Ji and Xia.
translations.idiomatic: His progeny included Ji and the later-disgraced Xia.

sentences.zh: 躋字景雲，官至散騎常侍。

translations.literal: Ji courtesy name Jingyun; office reached Cavalier Attendant-in-Ordinary.
translations.idiomatic: Ji, courtesy name Jingyun, rose to Cavalier Attendant-in-Ordinary.

sentences.zh: 夏以貪污棄放於世。

translations.literal: Xia by corruption was cast aside in the world.
translations.idiomatic: Xia was disgraced for graft and cast out of public life.

sentences.zh: 弟智，字子房，貞素有兄風。

translations.literal: Younger brother Zhi, courtesy name Zifang, chaste and plain had elder brother’s style.
translations.idiomatic: His brother Zhi, courtesy name Zifang, was as upright and austere as Liu Shi himself.

sentences.zh: 少貧窶，每負薪自給，讀誦不輟，竟以儒行稱。

translations.literal: In youth poor, often carried firewood to supply himself, reading and reciting did not cease; in the end by Confucian conduct was praised.
translations.idiomatic: He grew up poor, hauled his own firewood, never stopped reading, and won renown as a Confucian gentleman.

sentences.zh: 曆中書黃門吏部郎，出為潁川太守。

translations.literal: Passed through Palace Secretariat Yellow Gate Ministry of Personnel Gentleman, went out as Yingchuan governor.
translations.idiomatic: He served in the Palace Secretariat, the Yellow Gates, and the Ministry of Personnel, then left the capital as governor of Yingchuan.

sentences.zh: 平原管輅嘗謂人曰：「吾與劉潁川兄弟語，使人神思清發，昏不假寐。

translations.literal: Guan Lu of Pingyuan once said to people, “I with Liu of Yingchuan brothers speak—makes people’s spirit thought clear and quick; at dusk need not feign sleep.”
translations.idiomatic: Guan Lu of Pingyuan once said, “Conversation with the Liu brothers of Yingchuan clears the mind so that evening needs no nap.”

sentences.zh: 自此之外，殆白日欲寢矣。

translations.literal: Beyond this, almost in broad daylight wish to sleep.”
translations.idiomatic: With anyone else I could nap in broad daylight.”

sentences.zh: 」入為秘書監，領南陽王師，加散騎常侍，遷侍中、尚書、太常。

translations.literal: ” He entered as Director of the Palace Library, headed Prince of Nanyang’s tutor, added Cavalier Attendant-in-Ordinary, promoted Palace Attendant, Master of Writing, Minister of Ceremonies.
translations.idiomatic: Zhi was recalled as Director of the Palace Library and tutor to the Prince of Nanyang, given the added title Cavalier Attendant-in-Ordinary, and rose to Palace Attendant, Master of Writing, and Minister of Ceremonies.

sentences.zh: 著《喪服釋疑論》，多所辨明。

translations.literal: Composed Mourning Garments Explaining Doubts Treatise; much was clarified.
translations.idiomatic: He wrote “Resolving Doubts on Mourning Dress,” clarifying many disputed points.

sentences.zh: 太康末卒，諡曰成。

translations.literal: At the end of Taikang died; posthumous name Cheng.
translations.idiomatic: He died toward the end of Taikang with the posthumous title “Cheng” (“Accomplished”).

sentences.zh: 高光，字宣茂，陳留圉城人，魏太尉柔之子也。

translations.literal: Gao Guang, courtesy name Xuanmao, was a man of Yucheng in Chenliu, son of Wei Grand Commandant Rou.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Guang, courtesy name Xuanmao, came from Yucheng in Chenliu and was the son of the Wei Grand Commandant Gao Rou.

sentences.zh: 光少習家業，明練刑理。

translations.literal: Guang in youth practiced family occupation, clearly versed in punishments and principles.
translations.idiomatic: From youth he studied his family’s legal tradition and mastered penal law.

sentences.zh: 初以太子舍人累遷尚書郎，出為幽州刺史、潁州太守。

translations.literal: At first as Crown Prince attendant promoted in stages to Gentleman of the Masters of Writing, went out as Inspector of You Province, Governor of Ying Province.
translations.idiomatic: He began as a crown prince’s attendant, rose to secretary in the Masters of Writing, then served as Inspector of You and governor of Ying commandery.

sentences.zh: 是時武帝置黃沙獄，以典詔囚。

translations.literal: At this time Emperor Wu established Yellow Sand prison, to manage edict prisoners.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu had just founded the Yellow Sand prison for inmates sentenced by imperial edict.

sentences.zh: 以光曆世明法，用為黃沙御史，秩與中丞同，遷廷尉。

translations.literal: Because Guang through generations understood law, employed him as Yellow Sand censor; rank same as Palace Assistant Secretary; promoted Director of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: Given the family’s legal expertise, Guang was named censor of the Yellow Sand prison with rank equal to the Palace Assistant Secretary, then promoted Director of Justice.

sentences.zh: 元康中，拜尚書，典三公曹。

translations.literal: In Yuankang, appointed Master of Writing, managed Three Dukes bureau.
translations.idiomatic: During Yuankang he became a Master of Writing in charge of the Three Dukes section.

sentences.zh: 時趙王倫篡逆，光於其際，守道全貞。

translations.literal: When Prince of Zhao Lun usurped rebellion, Guang at that juncture kept the Way and preserved integrity.
translations.idiomatic: When Prince of Zhao Sima Lun seized power, Guang held to principle and kept his honor intact.

sentences.zh: 及倫賜死，齊王冏輔政，復以光為廷尉，遷尚書，加奉車都尉。

translations.literal: When Lun was ordered to die, Prince of Qi Jiong assisted governance, again made Guang Director of Justice, promoted Master of Writing, added Commandant of Court Carriages.
translations.idiomatic: After Lun was forced to kill himself, Prince of Qi Sima Jiong became regent and reappointed Guang Director of Justice, then Master of Writing with the added title Commandant of Court Carriages.

sentences.zh: 後從駕討成都王穎有勳，封延陵縣公，邑千八百戶。

translations.literal: Later following the carriage campaigning against Prince of Chengdu Ying had merit, enfeoffed Duke of Yanling county, fief one thousand eight hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: He later accompanied the emperor against Prince of Chengdu Sima Ying and earned a dukedom of Yanling county with eighteen hundred households.

sentences.zh: 于時朝廷咸推光明于用法，故頻典理官。

translations.literal: At that time the court all pushed Guang as enlightened in applying law; therefore repeatedly managed judicial offices.
translations.idiomatic: The court acknowledged his mastery of the law and repeatedly put him over the judiciary.

sentences.zh: 惠帝為張方所逼，幸長安，朝臣奔散，莫有從者，光獨侍帝而西。

translations.literal: Emperor Hui was pressed by Zhang Fang, favored Chang’an; court ministers fled scattered; none had followers; Guang alone attended the emperor west.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Hui was driven by Zhang Fang to take refuge in Chang’an and the court scattered, Guang alone followed him west.

sentences.zh: 遷尚書左僕射，加散騎常侍。

translations.literal: Promoted Left Vice Director of the Masters of Writing, added Cavalier Attendant-in-Ordinary.
translations.idiomatic: He was made Left Vice Director of the Masters of Writing and Cavalier Attendant-in-Ordinary.

sentences.zh: 光兄誕為上官巳等所用，曆徐、雍二州刺史。

translations.literal: Guang’s elder brother Dan was used by Shangguan Si and others, passed through Xu and Yong two provinces’ Inspectors.
translations.idiomatic: Guang’s elder brother Dan served Shangguan Si’s faction and held successive terms as Inspector of Xu and Yong.

sentences.zh: 誕性任放無倫次，而決烈過人，與光異操。

translations.literal: Dan’s nature was unrestrained without order, yet decisive fierceness surpassed others; with Guang different conduct.
translations.idiomatic: Dan was reckless and disorderly yet bolder than most—a temper utterly unlike his brother’s.

sentences.zh: 常謂光小節，恆輕侮之，光事誕愈謹。

translations.literal: He always called Guang petty punctilios, constantly slighted and insulted him; Guang served Dan more careful.
translations.idiomatic: He sneered at Guang as fussy and treated him with contempt, yet Guang treated him with growing deference.

sentences.zh: 帝既還洛陽，時太弟新立，重選傅訓，以光為少傅，加光祿大夫，常侍如故。

translations.literal: When the emperor had returned Luoyang, at the time the imperial younger brother was newly established, heavily selected tutors and instructors, made Guang Junior Tutor, added Grand Master of Splendid Happiness, attendant-in-ordinary as before.
translations.idiomatic: After the emperor’s return to Luoyang, with a new heir designate named, Guang was chosen Junior Tutor with the added title Grand Master of Splendid Happiness while keeping his position as attendant-in-ordinary.

sentences.zh: 及懷帝即位，加光祿大夫金章紫綬，與傅祗並見推崇。

translations.literal: When Emperor Huai ascended, added Grand Master of Splendid Happiness gold seal purple ribbon, with Fu Zhi together seen honored.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Huai added the gold seal and purple ribbon to his Splendid Happiness title and ranked him with Fu Zhi among the most honored ministers.

sentences.zh: 尋為尚書令，本官如故。

translations.literal: Soon was Director of the Masters of Writing; original offices as before.
translations.idiomatic: He soon became Director of the Masters of Writing while retaining his other posts.

sentences.zh: 以疾卒，贈司空、侍中。

translations.literal: By illness died; posthumously gifted Minister of Works, Palace Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: He died of illness and was posthumously named Minister of Works and Palace Attendant.

sentences.zh: 屬京洛傾覆，竟未加諡。

translations.literal: Happening that Jing-Luo overturned, in the end posthumous name was not added.
translations.idiomatic: Luoyang’s fall followed so quickly that no posthumous title was ever conferred.

sentences.zh: 子韜字子遠，放佚無檢。

translations.literal: Son Tao courtesy name Ziyuan, unrestrained without restraint.
translations.idiomatic: His son Tao, courtesy name Ziyuan, was dissolute and undisciplined.

sentences.zh: 光為廷尉時，韜受貨賕，有司奏案之，而光不知。

translations.literal: When Guang was Director of Justice, Tao received goods and bribes; responsible offices memorialized investigating him, yet Guang did not know.
translations.idiomatic: While Guang headed the court of justice, Tao took bribes; the authorities impeached him, yet Guang knew nothing of it.

sentences.zh: 時人雖非光不能防閑其子，以其用心有素，不以為累。

translations.literal: People of the time although blamed Guang for not being able to guard and restrain his son, because his intentions had long been plain, did not consider it a stain.
translations.idiomatic: Critics faulted him for failing to rein in his son, yet his lifelong integrity spared him lasting blame.

sentences.zh: 初，光詣長安留台，以韜兼右衛將軍。

translations.literal: At first, when Guang went to Chang’an residual headquarters, made Tao concurrent Right Guard general.
translations.idiomatic: When Guang went to the provisional administration at Chang’an, he had Tao named concurrent general of the Right Guard.

sentences.zh: 韜與殿省小人交通，及光卒，仍於喪中往來不絕。

translations.literal: Tao associated with palace petty men; when Guang died, still during mourning went back and forth without cease.
translations.idiomatic: Tao consorted with low palace cliques and, even during mourning for his father, kept up those visits without pause.

sentences.zh: 時東海王越輔政，不朝觀。

translations.literal: At the time Prince of East Sea Yue assisted governance, did not attend court audiences.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Yue of Donghai was regent then and rarely appeared at formal court.

sentences.zh: 韜知人心有望，密與太傅參軍薑賾、京兆杜概等謀討越，事泄伏誅。

translations.literal: Tao knew people’s hearts had resentment, secretly with Grand Tutor aide Jiang Ze, Jingzhao Du Gai and others plotted to punish Yue; matter leaked and he was executed.
translations.idiomatic: Tao sensed public hatred of Yue and secretly joined Grand Tutor staffer Jiang Ze, Du Gai of Jingzhao, and others in a plot against him; when it leaked, Tao was put to death.

sentences.zh: 史臣曰：下士競而文，中庸靜而質，不若進不足而退有餘也。

translations.literal: The historian says: Lower gentlemen strive and ornament; the middle path is quiet and substance—not like advancing insufficient and retreating sufficient.
translations.idiomatic: The historians write: petty men scramble for polish, the steady man keeps to plain substance—better to fall short in ambition than to overreach in holding power.

sentences.zh: 魏舒、劉寔發慮精華，結綬登槐，覽止成務。

translations.literal: Wei Shu, Liu Shi emitted thought’s essence, tied ribbons ascended locust, viewed stop completed tasks.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Shu and Liu Shi brought keen minds to the council hall beneath the locusts and saw great affairs through to completion.

sentences.zh: 季和切問近對，當官正色。

translations.literal: Jihe cutting questions near answers; holding office stern countenance.
translations.idiomatic: Li Xi answered hard questions face to face and kept a fearless mien in office.

sentences.zh: 詩云「貪人敗類」，豈劉夏之謂歟！

translations.literal: The Odes says ‘Greedy men ruin the kind’—how could it mean Liu Xia!”
translations.idiomatic: The Odes call greedy men the ruin of their kind—did they mean Liu Xia?”

sentences.zh: 贊曰：舒言不矜，憙對千乘。

translations.literal: Encomium says: Shu’s words not boastful; Xi confronted thousand-chariots.
translations.idiomatic: In praise: Wei Shu spoke without swagger; Li Xi faced down the mighty.

sentences.zh: 子真、宣茂，雅志難陵。

translations.literal: Zizhen, Xuanmao—refined will hard to encroach.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Zizhen and Gao Xuanmao—noble purpose none could bend.

sentences.zh: 進忠能舉，退讓攸興。

translations.literal: Advancing loyalty able to raise; retreating yielding thereby rises.
translations.idiomatic: They advanced loyalty and lifted the worthy, yielded office and let virtue flourish.

sentences.zh: 皎皎瑚器，來光玉繩。

translations.literal: Bright bright coral vessels; come light jade cord.
translations.idiomatic: Bright as ritual coral, they brought luster to the constellations of state.
